The 245-page report sets out the regulator’s assessment of the financial health of the game and provides an early indication of how interventionist it may be in applying its licensing powers. As a draft publication, the IFR must consider any responses before issuing its final report by May 2027.

The report sets out the IFR’s view that English football is in poor financial health at all levels of the game. This must be accompanied by action that will reduce financial risk, but changes should not undermine the success of the game.

bullets: Singers JJ Lin, Tia Ray and Lil Ghost performed at the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix on 9 October 2026 as part of Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME)'s efforts to bring Chinese-language artists to international stages. Tia Ray performed tracks including "Love Herby" and "Beautiful Day", while Lil Ghost gave the live world premiere of "Wild Card" from his album "KUI". JJ Lin closed the night on the main stage with a 20-song show involving a 100-member international team, after nearly six months of preparation, and debuted his English-language single "RISE WITHOUT A SOUND".

The performances drew a positive response from the artists and fans, and the sets of Tia Ray and Lil Ghost generated attention on Chinese social media, with many fans saying they intended to travel to Singapore the following year. JJ Lin, a long-time Formula 1 enthusiast, described the appearance in his home country as a dream stage. Wider Sports News.copy:
, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JJ Lin, Tia Ray and Lil Ghost brought their distinctive sounds to the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix on October 9, 2026, energizing the evening's entertainment in Singapore with performances that brought music and motorsport together for a global audience. The appearances were part of Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME)'s efforts to bring leading artists from the Chinese-language music scene to international stages.

Chinese R&B diva and acclaimed singer-songwriter Tia Ray performed signature tracks including "Love Herby" and "Beautiful Day", blending Eastern influences with international musical elements to highlight the distinctive sound and global outlook of Chinese R&B. She had recently headlined a solo show at the Grammy Museum, making her the first Chinese female singer to do so. Visionary singer-songwriter Lil Ghost performed material from his new album "KUI", staging the world live premiere of his track "Wild Card", backed by a full-band lineup and performing songs including "Saturday Night". His commanding stage presence energized the crowd. Together, the two artists showcased contemporary Chinese-language music through their distinct styles, drawing interest from music fans and motorsport enthusiasts around the world.

bullets: The English Football League and its 72 clubs are running the Together Against Racism campaign from 16 to 26 October, supported across two dedicated matchdays. It particularly urges supporters to report racist behaviour immediately through club channels, stewards or the police, rather than waiting until after a match. The campaign covers the Championship, League One and League Two.

EFL data from 2025/26 shows 63% of racism-related incidents reported live to clubs led to an individual being identified, with live reporting accounting for 85.7% of offender identifications. Supporters reporting during matches were 2.2 times more likely to see an offender identified. In total, 51 individuals received bans and 15 more were required to attend educational courses. Chief Executive Trevor Birch said more reporting gives a better chance of ensuring hate has consequences, and more than 550 supporters have taken part in Kick It Out fan education programmes.

All 13 EuroLeague Commercial Assets shareholder clubs approved the key economic aspects last week. The league is targeting €648m in annual commercial revenues by year 10 and expansion to 24 teams by the 2027-28 season.

The 13 shareholders also rejected an NBA offer to merge its NBA Europe proposal with the EuroLeague, although the door remains open to future offers. The NBA says it will launch the new league in 2027 regardless. Euroleague projects a 25% uplift in value from 2026-27 and expects all licensed clubs to be financially sustainable by the end of the plan's first phase, up from about 40% now.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Euroleague Basketball, the organizer of top European club competitions, has unveiled plans to distribute €3.4 billion ($3.8 billion) to participating teams over the next 10 years as part of a detailed long-term business plan after its shareholders rejected an offer to team up with the NBA.

The key economic aspects of Euroleague Basketball’s decade-long plan were approved by all 13 EuroLeague Commercial Assets (ECA) shareholder clubs late last week, with the organization seeking to press ahead with expansion plans.

bullets: Netflix will be the home of Fifa Women's World Cup coverage in the US and Canada for the 2027 and 2031 editions, with IMG named this month as its production partner for both. The first tournament is in Brazil, the second across the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. Netflix this week also announced rights to the 2030 Fifa World Cup in Spain, and now shows five NFL games a season, up from two last year.

Speaking at Leaders Week London, Netflix's Brandon Riegg said there was little debate about bidding when the rights went to market in 2024, given early live-sport performance and an existing documentary relationship with Fifa. IMG, now part of TKO Holdings, has already worked with Netflix on the Six Kings Slam tennis event in Saudi Arabia.
Wider Sports News.copy:

The global streaming giant now shows five National Football League (NFL) games a season, up from two last year. In December it will carry the most-hyped heavyweight boxing contest in a generation, as British former champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally collide at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium.

It confirms a directional shift for a platform that was long ambivalent about the value of expensive sports rights. More lies ahead, as Netflix moves from set-pieces to longer, more complex broadcast projects.

Wider Sports News.copy:
When Australia last hosted the Men’s Rugby World Cup in 2003, premium hospitality was largely defined by the basics: a great seat, quality food and the chance to entertain clients around a major sporting event.

Nearly 24 years later, expectations have changed dramatically. Today, premium guests are looking for access, authenticity and experiences that can’t be replicated anywhere else. The world’s biggest sporting events are no longer judged solely by what happens on the field, but by the moments they create around it. That shift has shaped every decision we’ve made while building the Rugby World Cup Experiences programme for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027.

bullets: Leicester Tigers fly-half Billy Searle, 30, turned down a potential return to France to stay at Welford Road, having agreed a new three-year deal in September. He joined from Agen for the start of 2025-26 and has previously played in France with Toulouse in 2022, Biarritz and Agen. He said he had interest from France but made clear to the club that his priority was to stay.

Searle said staying keeps him in contention for a first full England cap, to add to his England A appearance against Ireland in February. He cited informal conversations with head coach Steve Borthwick and noted that 2027 is a World Cup year. Tigers host Prem champions Northampton Saints on Saturday (15:05 BST) at a sold-out Welford Road, the first meeting since Saints won last season's semi-final on the way to the title.
Rugby.copy:
Leicester Tigers fly-half Billy Searle turned down a potential return to France to "push his game on" at Welford Road and stay on the radar for full England honours in the near future.

The former Bristol, Wasps and Worcester Warriors stand-off has had three spells playing French rugby in his career - a short stint at Toulouse in 2022, and with second-tier Biarritz and Agen - before moving back to England.

bullets: Scotland wing Duhan van der Merwe, 31, will play his first game of the season for Edinburgh against the Lions in the URC at Hive Stadium on Friday, after 18 months of injury problems that began with an ankle injury in March 2025. He had ankle surgery to be available for last year's British and Irish Lions tour of Australia, scoring five tries in five non-Test games, and was limited to 11 Edinburgh games last season.

Head coach Sean Everitt said Van der Merwe has trained exceptionally well, but that it is too soon to discuss international selection before Scotland coach Gregor Townsend names his squad on Monday for the November Tests against New Zealand, Australia and Japan. Darcy Graham misses the game with a calf strain. The match follows the death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, from natural causes the day before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland wing Duhan van der Merwe will aim to put 18 months of injury hassles behind him on Friday when he plays his first game of the season for Edinburgh in their URC match against the Lions at Hive Stadium.

The 31-year-old has endured a challenging time with fitness and form since suffering an ankle injury in March 2025. Van der Merwe had surgery on his ankle in order to be available for last year’s British and Irish Lions tour of Australia, but was never in serious contention for the Test matches despite five tries in five other games he played.

bullets: Australia coach Les Kiss has named a settled side for the first Bledisloe Cup Test against New Zealand at Eden Park on Saturday, keeping Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the left wing rather than restoring him to midfield. Queensland Reds centre Isaac Henry, 27, is the only change, starting at outside centre because Hunter Paisami is banned for four weeks for a high tackle against South Africa. Len Ikitau moves to No 12 after passing an ankle fitness test.

The All Blacks are without fly-half Richie Mo'unga, who tore a calf muscle and will miss both Tests, and winger Fehi Fineanganofo, who failed concussion tests. Coach Dave Rennie moves Damian McKenzie to No 10 and names Beauden Barrett at fullback, with Scott Barrett starting in the second row. Rugby.copy:

Four-Test Queensland Reds midfielder Henry will start at outside centre in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park on Saturday, two months after making his debut against Japan in Osaka.

The return of 27-year-old Henry is the only change to the starting side who upset South Africa 42-38 in Perth two weeks ago. Inside centre Hunter Paisami received a four-week ban for a high tackle against the world champions and is not available.

Rugby.title: Maro Itoje seals England future by agreeing new deal with Saracens
Rugby.summary: Maro Itoje seals England future by agreeing new deal with Saracens The Guardian
bullets: Maro Itoje has agreed a new deal with Saracens, believed to run until 2029, rejecting interest from Top 14 clubs, with Perpignan and Bordeaux among those mooted. His existing contract, signed in 2024, was due to expire after next year's World Cup. The 31-year-old, who has 102 caps, first played for the club in 2013.

Saracens' Brendan Venter, back in charge for a second time, said Itoje had agreed terms with the owner and described him as a brilliant leader. Itoje was rested for England's summer Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, and had his first full pre-season with Saracens since 2014. He was among the first players given an enhanced England contract, worth £150,000, in 2024, although none of the existing deals run beyond the World Cup in Australia next year.
Rugby.copy:
Maro Itoje has reaffirmed his long‑term commitment to England, rejecting interest from France by agreeing a new deal with Saracens. Itoje’s existing deal, signed in 2024, was due to expire after the World Cup next year but he has agreed terms with his club despite interest from Top 14 sides. A move to either Perpignan or Bordeaux had been mooted but the 31-year-old is to commit his future to the club he first represented in 2013 with a new deal, believed to be until 2029.

The extension is a significant boost for Saracens, who are in a period of transition with Brendan Venter at the helm for a second time and will enable Itoje, who has 102 caps, to continue his international career. It remains to be seen whether Steve Borthwick will still be in charge of the England side but either the national head coach or his successor is to benefit.

Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: ‘Freer’ Red Roses resolve to come back stronger after Canada end epic run
Rugby.summary: ‘Freer’ Red Roses resolve to come back stronger after Canada end epic run The Guardian
bullets: England's Red Roses suffered their first defeat in four years when Canada beat them, ending a run of 40 wins and one draw. The sides meet again this weekend. England have lost only twice in 73 matches over the past seven years.

Head coach John Mitchell, who lost his first game in charge, said a setback generally helps a team learn quicker and that the players may feel "freer" with the unbeaten run over. Captain Meg Jones said the key message was for the squad to stick together and respond. The loss, England's first away from home since the 2022 World Cup final, is seen as useful preparation for defending the title at the 2029 World Cup in Australia.
Rugby.copy:
England’s glittering unbeaten era is over. Canada defeated the Red Roses to deal them a first defeat in four years after 40 wins and one draw. It was a landmark result for the Canadians, who will look to replicate the outcome this weekend when the two nations meet again. England must reset but they won’t panic; the Red Roses have been the standard bearers for the past seven years, which is why they have lost only twice in 73 matches. But while no team would ever aim to lose, falling to defeat is a good thing for England and the wider sport.

Losing could actually make England a deadlier team to face. That is because they now need to find another level to their game with teams beginning to figure out ways to beat them. They have been pushed over the past few years by teams such as Canada, New Zealand and France, but they always had just enough to get the result over the line. Now they have been presented with a new challenge and John Mitchell, who lost his first game as Red Roses head coach, said post-defeat when his side “gets a setback, it generally learns quicker”.

Rugby.copy:
The Hurricanes have signed a one-year contract extension with 23-year-old playmaker Harry Godfrey, who has recently returned to the field after missing the entire 2026 Super season with a major knee injury.

Godfrey’s contract wasn’t set to expire until after the 2027 season, but he and the Hurricanes have put pen to paper early to secure his future in Wellington. The Hawke’s Bay product has made 16 Hurricanes appearances since his 2023 debut, with his breakthrough 2025 campaign cruelly cut short by injury, while a subsequent torn ACL then ended his 2025 NPC season and ruled him out of the 2026 Super Rugby season entirely.

Rugby.title: Exclusive Wallaroos club set to welcome new member against Scotland
Rugby.summary: Eva Karpani is set to join Michaela Leonard in an incredibly exclusive Wallaroos club this week by bringing up 50 Test caps for Australia.
bullets: Eva Karpani is set to win her 50th Test cap for the Wallaroos when Australia face Scotland on Friday in their final WXV Global Series match, again coming off the bench. The tighthead prop debuted against Japan in 2019 and is the third-top try-scorer in Wallaroos history. She will join Michaela Leonard in the exclusive 50-cap club.

Australia are seeking a third consecutive win after beating Scotland 30-19 in Edinburgh last month and 56-12 at Sydney's Accor Stadium on Saturday. Deisree Miller is out with a calf injury, so Faitala Moleka moves to fullback and Cecilia Smith starts at inside centre. Emily Chancellor will play her 42nd and final Test.
Rugby.copy:
Eva Karpani is set to join Michaela Leonard in an incredibly exclusive Wallaroos club this week, with the veteran front-rower set to bring up 50 Test caps. Karpani will again provide impact off the bench when Australia faces Scotland on Friday evening.

Karpani debuted in Wallaroos gold against Japan in 2019 and has been a matchday regular for the national team ever since. The tighthead prop is the third-top try-scorer in Wallaroos history, with outside backs Deisree Miller and Maya Stewart ahead on that list.

Rugby.summary: All Blacks greats Justin Marshall and Kieran Read have reacted to Beauden Barrett’s standout performance in the 43-21 win over the Wallabies.
Rugby.copy:
All Blacks greats Justin Marshall and Kieran Read have reacted to Beauden Barrett’s standout performance in the 43-21 win over the Wallabies, with the 147-Test veteran turning heads with a two-try effort at Accor Stadium.

Barrett didn’t feature at all during the Nations Championship Tests in July and played just nine minutes off the bench during the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series. But with Ruben Love and Richie Mo’unga unavailable, Dave Rennie turned to the experienced playmaker for the Bledisloe Cup.

Rugby.title: Three changes to Scotland team for Wallaroos clash as duo set for debuts
Rugby.summary: Three changes to Scotland team for Wallaroos clash as duo set for debuts Scotland Rugby News
bullets: Aicha Sutcliffe will make her first start for Scotland Women among three changes for the match against Australia in Canberra on Friday, with a 9.30am UK kick-off. Hannah Ramsay takes over at fly-half from Helen Nelson, who moves to inside centre, while Chloe Rollie returns at full-back and Meryl Smith replaces Evie Wills at 13.

Scotland, beaten heavily by the hosts in Sydney on Saturday, are seeking to end an eight-match winless run under Dave Butcher. Sutcliffe, who scored a try on her debut in the Women's Six Nations, replaces Lana Skeldon at hooker, and Sarah Bonar returns from illness in the second row for Hollie Cunningham. Nineteen-year-old tighthead Imogen Spence could win a first cap from the bench, and Nicole Flynn and Lucia Scott are also among the replacements.
Rugby.copy:
Aicha Sutcliffe will make her first start for Scotland among three changes to the side to face Australia in Canberra on Friday (9.30am kick-off UK time). After a drubbing by their hosts in Sydney on Saturday, Dave Butcher has handed opportunities to Sutcliffe and Hannah Ramsay, who takes over at fly-half from Helen Nelson, as Scotland seek to end an eight-match winless run.

Ramsay's positional switch - she started at fullback last weekend - means there is a return to the side for Chloe Rollie in the 15 shirt, while Nelson moves to inside centre and Meryl Smith takes over at 13 from Evie Wills, who is not in the matchday 23.

Rugby.title: Steve Hansen's 'inconvenient fact' for Les Kiss' Wallabies
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks coach Steve Hansen has identified what he calls an "inconvenient fact" holding the Wallabies back after another Bledisloe Cup series loss to the All Blacks.
Rugby.copy:
Former All Blacks coach Steve Hansen has identified what he calls an “inconvenient fact” holding the Wallabies back after another Bledisloe Cup series loss. Hansen, who spent 17 years with the All Blacks, including eight as head coach, oversaw much of what is now a 24-year reign as Bledisloe Cup holders. Much was made of Australia’s prospects coming into the 2026 edition of the rivalry after a famous win over South Africa, but New Zealand’s 93 points across the two Tests dwarfed Australia’s 40 and saw the Bledisloe Cup return to NZR’s trophy cabinet once again.

Reacting to the series on this week’s episode of the Rugby Unity podcast, Hansen addressed the Wallabies’ leadership, defending captain Harry Wilson by emphasising the communal nature of leadership responsibilities. Australia didn’t escape Hansen’s analysis without individual accountability, though.

Rugby.title: New Zealand legends react as All Blacks star retires with immediate effect
Rugby.summary: New Zealand legends react as All Blacks star retires with immediate effect Ruck.co.uk
bullets: Former All Blacks hooker Liam Coltman has retired from rugby with immediate effect at the age of 36. He announced the decision after Otago's NPC semi-final defeat to Northland, in which he played the final 13 minutes off the bench.

Coltman made his provincial debut in 2010 and joined the Highlanders in 2013, playing all 19 matches in their 2015 Super Rugby title win. He made his All Blacks debut against Italy in 2016, won eight Test caps and was in the 2019 Rugby World Cup squad. He also captained Otago and played for Lyon, the Utah Warriors and Canon Eagles. Former team-mates including Aaron Smith and Richie Mo'unga paid tribute, and Coltman said he plans to start work in the building trade next year.
Rugby.copy:
Former All Blacks hooker Liam Coltman has retired from rugby with immediate effect at the age of 36. Coltman announced his retirement after Otago's NPC semi-final defeat to Northland. He came off the bench and played the final 13 minutes of the match.

The hooker made his provincial debut in 2010 before joining the Highlanders' Super Rugby squad in 2013. He became their first-choice hooker the following season and played a key role in their historic 2015 title win, featuring in all 19 matches that campaign.

Rugby.title: Wales great Taulupe Faletau makes retirement decision
Rugby.summary: Wales great Taulupe Faletau makes retirement decision Ruck.co.uk
bullets: Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau, 35, has no plans to retire and still has the 2027 Rugby World Cup in mind, despite being left out of Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad after another injury setback. He returned for Cardiff against Northampton Saints on Sunday and played 55 minutes.

The 109-cap forward has not played for Wales since facing Japan in 2025, with knee and calf injuries keeping him out. Tandy said he would not rule anyone out and has spoken to Faletau about being fit and available, adding that they can decide once he has put together consistent rugby. Faletau would be 36 when the 2027 tournament begins in Australia, and he has yet to confirm when he will retire.
Rugby.copy:
Wales legend Taulupe Faletau has no plans to hang up his boots just yet, with one last Rugby World Cup still on his mind. The 35-year-old missed out on Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad after another injury setback.

But the 109-cap star may still have one final chapter left in him. Faletau made his return for Cardiff against Northampton Saints on Sunday. He played 55 minutes and showed he has lost none of his class.

Rugby.title: Janse van Rensburg agrees new Bristol deal
Rugby.summary: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg, 29, signs a new contract with Bristol Bears.
bullets: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg has signed a new contract with Bristol Bears, although the Prem club have not confirmed the length of the 29-year-old's deal. It is his third deal with the club in a little over three years, after joining from London Irish in June 2023 and extending in November 2025.

Janse van Rensburg qualified for England on residency grounds in July and scored on his international debut against Fiji. He is currently in return-to-play protocols after being stretchered off in the win against Northampton, and could be available to face Exeter Chiefs on Saturday. Bristol director of rugby Pat Lam described him as one of the best players he has coached.
Rugby.copy:
England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg has signed a new contract with Bristol Bears. The Prem club have not confirmed the length of the 29-year-old's deal. "I've really enjoyed the way we play rugby here," Janse van Rensburg told Bristol's website.

"It suits my game, gives me the freedom to express myself and challenges me to keep improving." Janse van Rensburg started Bristol's first two matches of the season but is currently going through return-to-play protocols after being stretchered off following a collision during their win against Northampton earlier this month.

Rugby.title: 'One of the best' Benhard Janse van Rensburg pledges future to Bristol
Rugby.summary: The England centre has decided to extend his stay at the Bears beyond the end of this season.
bullets: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg has signed a new contract with Bristol Bears, committing his future to the club. The South African-born midfielder joined in 2023 from London Irish, is approaching 75 competitive appearances for Bristol and made his England Test debut in July during the Nations Championship.

Director of Rugby Pat Lam described him as one of the best players he has coached, citing his consistency, attitude and the high standards he sets in training and on matchdays. Janse van Rensburg said staying was an easy decision, pointing to the squad's ambition, the style of rugby Bristol play and the support shown to him and his family.

Rugby.title: Amy Cokayne: Red Roses not at 'panic stations' after Canada defeat
Rugby.summary: England vice-captain Amy Cokayne has insisted that the team are not at "panic stations" after their WXV Global Series loss to Canada.
bullets: England vice-captain Amy Cokayne has said the Red Roses are not at "panic stations" after losing 24-21 to Canada in the WXV Global Series at BMO Field. Shoshanah Seumanutafa's 78th-minute try decided the match and ended England's 41-match unbeaten run, their first defeat since the 2021 Rugby World Cup final against New Zealand.

The sides meet again on Friday night at Ottawa's TD Place, which Cokayne said gives England an unusual chance to respond against the same opposition. She said the squad had analysed the loss and identified small execution errors to fix. England finish 2026 against the USA in New Jersey on Friday 30 October. Jess Breach suffered her first defeat on her 60th cap.
Rugby.copy:
England vice-captain Amy Cokayne has insisted that the Red Roses are not at “panic stations” after their WXV Global Series loss to Canada. Shoshanah Seumanutafa’s 78th-minute try proved to be the difference between the two teams as Kévin Rouet’s side registered a 24-21 win.

The defeat at BMO Field ended the Red Roses’ 41-match unbeaten run, their first loss since the 2021 Rugby World Cup final against New Zealand at Eden Park. Due to face Canada again this Friday night at Ottawa’s TD Place, the Red Roses have an opportunity to register an immediate response.

Rugby.title: Saracens owner backs CEO and rejects chaos claims
Rugby.summary: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has full confidence in CEO Ed Coetzee, rejecting claims of "executive-level chaos".
bullets: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester has said he has "full confidence" in chief executive Ed Coetzee, rejecting a Times article that claimed the club was suffering "executive-level chaos". In an open letter on the club's website, Silvester said Coetzee had achieved an "extraordinary amount" since being appointed in July. The Times had pointed to Coetzee being the third chief executive in two years and alleged high staff turnover.

Silvester cited Coetzee's achievements, including bringing the all-female athletics meeting Athlos and the Mayo v Kerry Gaelic football fixture to StoneX Stadium, as well as new commercial and hospitality partnerships. He also highlighted a strengthened executive team, with Jason Thomas as chief financial officer and Rob Cook as chief operating officer, and said the board was committed to financial sustainability.
Rugby.copy:
Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has "full confidence" in chief executive Ed Coetzee and dismissed a newspaper article suggesting there was "executive-level chaos" at the club.

In an open letter on Saracens' website, external, responding to an article in The Times last week, Silvester said Coetzee had achieved an "extraordinary amount" since being appointed in July.

Rugby.title: Blitzboks go again with ‘target on our backs’
Rugby.summary: Blitzboks go again with ‘target on our backs’ News24
bullets: The 2026-27 SVNS Series opens in Dubai on 28 and 29 November, with the Cape Town leg the following weekend. The Blitzboks arrive as world champions for a second consecutive season, having won the title in June. They also won the league standings and five of the nine tournaments last season, including a second successive Cape Town victory.

Forward Zain Davids, who has played in 60 SVNS Series tournaments, said the team expects to carry a target as the top side, with rivals analysing them closely. The season also offers qualification for the 2028 Olympics in the United States: the top four in the World Championship standings qualify automatically, as do the winners of six continental tournaments. The 12th place goes to a last-chance qualifier, and the United States has already qualified as host.
Rugby.copy:
- The Blitzboks enter the new World Rugby Sevens season full of confidence following a successful campaign. - The new season starts at the end of the month in Dubai. - The home leg will once again be staged at Cape Town Stadium in December.

- For more rugby news, visit our dedicated section. Despite the many successes the Blitzboks have achieved over the past two seasons, there is no danger of the team getting carried away.

Rugby.title: Wales great Faletau still has drive for fourth World Cup
Rugby.summary: Wales boss Steve Tandy believes Taulupe Faletau is a World Cup contender despite missing out on the Nations Championship squad.
bullets: Wales head coach Steve Tandy believes number eight Taulupe Faletau, 35, is still driven by the prospect of a fourth World Cup. Faletau was left out of the squad for the Nations Championship after only returning from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on Sunday, where he played 55 minutes. He has 109 Wales caps but has not played under Tandy, and has not won a cap since facing Japan in the summer of 2025.

Tandy said he would not rule anyone out and had spoken to Faletau about being fit and available, but wants evidence of durability before a World Cup squad of 33 is chosen. Faletau has played only 31 times for Cardiff since joining from Bath in 2022. He could feature in November's Tests in Cardiff, and Cardiff host Sharks in the URC on Friday before facing Ospreys.
Rugby.copy:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy believes legendary number eight Taulupe Faletau is still fuelled by playing at a fourth World Cup. The 35-year-old was left out of Wales' squad for the Nations Championship, having only made his return from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on Sunday.

Faletau showed his class during a 55-minute appearance against the English champions but will remain with Cardiff rather than hunting a first cap since facing Japan in the summer of 2025.

Rugby.title: Jon Flatman: Cardiff Rugby appoint Barnsley FC chief executive as new CEO
Rugby.summary: Jon Flatman: Cardiff Rugby appoint Barnsley FC chief executive as new CEO BBC
bullets: Cardiff Rugby have appointed Barnsley FC chief executive Jon Flatman as their new CEO, with him due to start in January. The club have been without a full-time CEO since Richard Holland left the role 18 months ago, and managing director Jamie Muir will continue to lead the company until Flatman arrives.

Flatman said his priorities are taking the club back into private, independent ownership and resolving a long-term future at Cardiff Arms Park. Cardiff are still owned by the Welsh Rugby Union. He joined Barnsley in 2023 as chief revenue officer and became permanent CEO in 2024, helping to secure a long-term lease and development at Oakwell and sitting on the EFL board for League One clubs. Barnsley chairman Neerav Parekh said recruitment of a replacement is under way.
Rugby.copy:
Cardiff Rugby have appointed Barnsley Football Club's chief executive officer Jon Flatman as their new CEO. Flatman will assume the role in January and says he will prioritise securing private, independent ownership and establishing a long-term future at Cardiff Arms Park.

During his time at Barnsley, Flatman played a role in securing a long-term lease and development at Oakwell Stadium, and served on the English Football League (EFL) board as a representative of League One clubs.

Rugby.title: Five Wales stars not on flight to South Africa and Springbok's contract terminated
Rugby.summary: Five Wales stars not on flight to South Africa and Springbok's contract terminated Wales Online
bullets: The Scarlets have left five Wales internationals, Ryan Elias, Sam Costelow, Eddie James, Ellis Mee and Blair Murray, at home as the squad travelled to South Africa for United Rugby Championship matches against the Stormers in Cape Town on 24 October and the Bulls in Pretoria on 31 October. The club said the decision, agreed with the WRU, forms part of the player-management and rest provisions of PRA25 ahead of the Autumn Nations Championship.

The Scarlets travel with a 30-man squad, boosted by new signing Tom Allen and the return of prop Corey Domachowski. Separately, Springboks flanker Kwagga Smith, 32, has left Japanese club Shizuoka Blue Revs after eight seasons, with his contract terminated by mutual agreement as he recovers from injury. He joined in 2018 when the club were known as Yamaha Jubilo, and has won 63 caps for South Africa.
Rugby.copy:
Here are the latest rugby headlines this evening following the announcement of the Wales autumn squad. Five Wales internationals have been left at home by the Scarlets as the rest of the squad flew to South Africa today for matches against the Stormers and Bulls.

Ryan Elias, Sam Costelow, Eddie James, Ellis Mee and Blair Murray will miss the United Rugby Championship matches as part of planned recovery provisions agreed with the Welsh Rugby Union.

Rugby.title: Rugby Sevens set for historic return at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Rugby Sevens set for historic return at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Primedia Plus
bullets: Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time at Dakar 2026 in Senegal. The tournament starts on 1 November at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop, one day after the opening ceremony on 31 October, with medals awarded on 2 and 3 November.

Eight men's and eight women's teams will be split into two pools of four. In the men's competition, hosts Senegal are in Pool A with South Africa, Canada and Germany, while Pool B features Argentina, France, Japan and Samoa. Dakar 2026 will be the first Olympic sporting event held in Africa, with around 2,700 athletes across 25 sports, and the first Youth Olympic Games to use the IOC's updated sports framework.
Rugby.copy:
Rugby ball resting on a field. Photo: Pexels/Pablo Hsm Dakar 2026 will make history as the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the African continent. Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time when the world's best young players compete at Dakar 2026 in Senegal.

The tournament will kick off on November 1 at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop, just one day after the opening ceremony on October 31. Medals will be awarded on November 2 and 3.

Rugby.title: The buzz of winning? No, Newcastle boss McFarland prefers Mondays
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland on why winning cannot be the sole motivator for his group of players.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland, 54, says he prefers Mondays to Saturdays whether his side have won or lost, arguing that a professional's purpose cannot be winning alone. He took over a squad with 25 new players after the club finished bottom of the league in each of the last four seasons. They have lost all three opening Prem games but taken four bonus points, sitting ninth, two points above bottom side Harlequins.

McFarland said Mondays let him use the week's debrief and analysis to build an action plan for improvement, a view he formed as a player after moving from Stade Francais to Connacht. Ahead of Friday's game against Sale Sharks, he has shown his players footage of Michael Jordan's Chicago Bulls overcoming a 15-point fourth-quarter deficit against Portland Trail Blazers in the 1992 NBA Finals, to illustrate resilience.
Rugby.copy:
When we think of sport, the image that comes to mind is of incredible goals or brilliant tries or spell-bounding points that contribute to success. They are the things that stay with us, but as moments in themselves, they are fleeting, usually nothing more than a matter of seconds.

But the mantra we're lead to believe is that sport, especially at the highest level, is all about winning. Yet Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland is cut from a different cloth. For him, it is not winning but the constant search for self-improvement on an individual and team level that is his prime motivating factor.

bullets: Munster Rugby have confirmed that centre Alex Nankivell has signed a two-year contract extension, keeping him at the province until at least 2029. The uncapped 29-year-old joined from the Chiefs in the summer of 2023 and has made 58 Munster appearances. Last season he played 20 games and won three Player of the Match awards, and he also featured for the Barbarians against South Africa and Wales.

Nankivell won both the Bank of Ireland Men's Player of the Year and Virgin Media Supporters' Players of the Year awards at the 2026 Munster Rugby Awards. Munster general manager Ian Costello described him as a highly valued and respected squad member and said the club was delighted he had committed his future. Costello added that Nankivell has international ambitions and the club hopes he realises them in the near future.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: Exeter Chiefs appoint coach with international experience ahead of new PWR season
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs Women have named vastly experienced Curtis Bradford as an assistant coach ahead of the new Premiership Women's Rugby season.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs Women have appointed Welshman Curtis Bradford as an assistant coach ahead of the new JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby season. He arrives from Rugby Deutschland after three and a half years, most recently as director of rugby for the men's XVs programme and head coach of the Germany women's sevens squad.

Bradford will lead the defence and work closely with the backs at Sandy Park. His earlier roles include posts with the Welsh Rugby Union, Kuala Lumpur Tigers, NSW Waratahs and the Austrian Rugby Union. Head coach Oli Bishop said he wants a more aggressive, connected defensive side. Exeter finished third in PWR last season and lost their play-off to eventual champions Saracens; they begin 2026/27 against Bristol Bears at Shaftesbury Park on Saturday 28 November in Round 2.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs Women have named vastly experienced Curtis Bradford as an assistant coach ahead of the new JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season. The Welshman arrives in Devon after three and a half years with Rugby Deutschland, where he most recently led the men’s XVs programme as director of rugby and served as head coach of the Germany women’s sevens squad. Previously, Bradford was the union’s skills coach.

Bradford has held coaching and development roles with the Welsh Rugby Union, Kuala Lumpur Tigers in Malaysia, NSW Waratahs and Austrian Rugby Union, alongside club coaching positions in Italy and Germany.

Rugby.title: Bath shed more light on Dan du Preez's injury
Rugby.summary: Bath Rugby have confirmed that new signing Dan du Preez will miss the club's next two PREM matches
bullets: Bath Rugby have confirmed that new signing Dan du Preez will miss the PREM matches away to Gloucester this Friday and at home to his former club Sale on Saturday 31 October. The 31-year-old injured his hamstring in training before last weekend's defeat to Montpellier in the Investec Champions Cup, having scored tries in both his appearances so far, against Harlequins and Exeter.

Miles Reid, who missed the Montpellier match with concussion, is nearing completion of his return-to-play protocol and is expected to be available this weekend. Sam Underhill is out until at least December with a bicep injury. Will Muir, Henry Arundell and Tom de Glanville have resumed elements of training. Billy Sela returns in late November, Jamie Bhatti is targeting the New Year, and Thompson Cowan is on track for the Autumn Prem Cup block, which begins away to Exeter on 7 November.
Rugby.copy:
Bath Rugby have confirmed that new signing Dan du Preez will miss the club’s next two PREM matches, the away trip to Gloucester this Friday and the clash at home to his former club Sale on Saturday 31 October.

Du Preez, who has had a solid enough start to his Bath career following a close-season move, injured his hamstring in training ahead of last weekend’s defeat to Montpellier in the Investec Champions Cup.

Rugby.title: Leicester duo snubbed by Wales in latest squad announcement
Rugby.summary: Leicester back-rowers Tommy Reffell and Olly Cracknell have missed out on selection for Wales’ upcoming Nations Championship campaign.
bullets: Steve Tandy has named a 39-man Wales squad for games against Japan, New Zealand and Australia and a closing fixture at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on finals weekend. Leicester's Tommy Reffell and Cracknell miss out despite good form in the Gallagher Prem, while club teammates Aaron Wainwright and Gabe Hamer-Webb are included.

Uncapped trio Aneurin Owen, Che Hope and Rhys Barratt are in a squad with an average age of 27, including 14 England-based players and one in France. Faletau, who turns 36 in November, and Saracens centre Nick Tompkins are also absent. Liam Belcher, Tomas Francis, Archie Griffin, Louie Hennessey and Dafydd Jenkins return after missing the July window. Tandy said Principality Stadium means an awful lot to the players.
Rugby.copy:
Steve Tandy has named a 39-man squad for games against Japan, New Zealand and Australia and a closing fixture at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on finals weekend. Reffell and Cracknell’s club teammates, Aaron Wainwright and Gabe Hamer-Webb, have made the cut.

Meanwhile, uncapped trio Aneurin Owen, Che Hope and Rhys Barrett are included in a squad with an average age of 27, and boasting 14 players based in England and one in France.

Rugby.title: Irish provinces on red alert as South African centre considers switch
Rugby.summary: A physical, direct, and highly competitive midfielder who can also play 13, Jonathan Roche was part of the Stormers side that played the All Blacks on the Greatest Rivalry Tour this summer.
bullets: Stormers inside centre Jonathan Roche, 23, is weighing up a switch of international allegiance to Ireland, for which he qualifies through his paternal grandmother. Out of contract at the end of the season, the Cape Town-born centre has put Irish provinces on alert, and scored his first two senior tries in the 49-12 Champions Cup win over Bristol Bears last weekend.

Roche, who can also play at 13, was in the Stormers side that faced the All Blacks on the Greatest Rivalry Tour this summer and received an invitation to a Springbok alignment camp in 2025. He could become a long-term successor to Bundee Aki, 36, or Robbie Henshaw, 33. Other South Africans have moved to Ireland, with Ulster signing Rynard Gordon and Josh Neill joining Leinster's Academy.
Rugby.copy:
Stormers inside centre Jonathan Roche, who is out of contract at the end of the season, has put Irish Provinces on red alert after it has been revealed that he is weighing up a switch of international allegiance.

Cape Town-born Roche, 23, qualifies for an Irish passport through his grandmother on his father’s side of the family. A physical, direct, and highly competitive midfielder who can also play 13, Roche was part of the Stormers side that played the All Blacks on the Greatest Rivalry Tour this summer.

Rugby.title: British & Irish Lions Women confirm three key appointments with 'wealth of experience'
Rugby.summary: The British & Irish Lions have made three key appointments as the countdown to their inaugural Women's Tour next year gathers pace.
bullets: The British & Irish Lions have made three appointments ahead of their inaugural Women's Tour next year: Charlie Hayter as general manager of high performance, Josie Symonds as head of athletic performance and Eimear Flannery as head of operations. Hayter joins on secondment from the RFU, where he has been head of women's performance since 2023, part-time immediately, joining the Lions Executive team in January and going full-time from March.

Symonds joins on secondment from the Scottish Rugby Union, full-time from January, to oversee the tour's athletic performance programme. Flannery previously worked with the Irish Rugby Football Union and Edinburgh Rugby and will lead operational and logistical delivery. Hayter's immediate priority is the 2027 Women's Tour, followed by preparations for the 2029 men's tour. Head coach Jo Yapp said their experience would lay a foundation for the next 12 months.
Rugby.copy:
The British & Irish Lions have made three key appointments as the countdown to their inaugural Women’s Tour next year gathers pace. The appointments include Charlie Hayter as general manager of high performance, Josie Symonds as head of athletic performance and Eimear Flannery as head of operations.

Jo Yapp, British & Irish Lions Women head coach, said: “I’m delighted to welcome Charlie, Josie and Eimear to The British & Irish Lions. They will bring a unique skill set and invaluable expertise to what we are creating ahead of next year’s Lions Women’s Tour.

Rugby.title: Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call
Rugby.summary: Wales include uncapped Dragons backs Aneurin Owen and Che Hope in the squad for November Nations Championship Tests but Taulupe Faletau misses out.
bullets: Wales head coach Steve Tandy has named a 39-strong squad for the November Nations Championship Tests, with hooker Dewi Lake as captain. Dragons centre Aneurin Owen and scrum-half Che Hope are included uncapped, alongside Cardiff loose-head prop Rhys Barratt, while Dragons lock Seb Davies, Cardiff number eight Taine Basham and Dragons wing Rio Dyer are called up.

Leicester flanker Tommy Reffell, who faces four to six weeks out with a knee injury, and Taulupe Faletau are among the notable absentees. Wales face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff and finish against a southern hemisphere opponent at Twickenham on finals weekend. Tandy said Owen's consistency and performances had earned his opportunity, while Hope comes in with Kieran Hardy facing a lengthy lay-off after a knee injury.
Rugby.copy:
Uncapped Dragons centre Aneurin Owen and scrum-half Che Hope have been included in Wales' squad for the Nations Championship. Steve Tandy has selected a 39-strong group for the November Tests, with hooker Dewi Lake named as captain.

The head coach calls up Dragons lock Seb Davies and Cardiff number eight Taine Basham for the first time since he took charge of the national side. Cardiff loose-head prop Rhys Barratt, who played in the summer fixture against the Barbarians, is the third uncapped player in the squad, while Dragons wing Rio Dyer earns a recall.

Rugby.title: Welsh rugby mourns as second-row Jack Davies dies aged 24
Rugby.summary: Welsh rugby mourns as second-row Jack Davies dies aged 24 Ruck.co.uk
Rugby.copy:
The rugby community is mourning the death of Clwb Rygbi Caernarfon and RGC second row Jack Davies, who has died aged just 24. Davies represented North Wales side RGC in Super Rygbi Cymru, as well as Caernarfon in Welsh Rugby Union Division One North.

He joined Clwb Rygbi Caernarfon at the age of 12, having shown great promise as a young athlete. He progressed through several teams before earning a place in the RGC pathway.

Rugby.title: Unshackled Freeman in Christian Wade's rear mirror as record approaches
Rugby.summary: A purple patch of form has left Wade one short of Ashton's 101-try landmark going into Friday night's Northern derby against Sale Sharks at Kingston Park.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls winger Christian Wade is one try short of Chris Ashton's PREM record of 101 tries going into Friday night's Northern derby against Sale Sharks at Kingston Park. The 35-year-old reached 100 with a hat-trick against Exeter in the third round earlier this month. Ashton set the record in 2023 while at Leicester, having overtaken Tom Varndell's 92 tries in 2022.

Northampton and England winger Tommy Freeman is the main threat to the record in the longer term. He joined Wade on five tries this season with a brace in the 71-48 win over Bath, and has 60 PREM tries from 89 appearances, a try every 1.48 games, the best strike rate among players with 50 or more tries. Sam Simmonds is second on 1.54, Wade third on 1.56 and Max Malins fourth on 1.59. Freeman's club-mate Ollie Sleightholme has 45 tries from 70 appearances and needs five more to reach 50.
Rugby.copy:
It would would appear to be a case of when, not if, Newcastle Red Bulls flyer Christian Wade breaks Chris Ashton’s longstanding PREM try-scoring record. A purple patch of form has left Wade one short of Ashton’s 101-try landmark going into Friday night’s Northern derby against Sale Sharks at Kingston Park.

Just as Ashton did in 2023 whilst seeing out his career at Leicester, dual code winger Wade brought up his century with a hat-trick against Exeter in the third round earlier this month.

Rugby.title: ‘If the Bledisloe Cup must be a two-Test series, why not put it up for grabs every match?’
Rugby.summary: After New Zealand retained the trophy for a 24th straight year, is it time to change the format?
bullets: Calls are growing in Australia and New Zealand for a change to the Bledisloe Cup format, with the suggestion that the trophy be contested in every match between the two nations while the series remains at two Tests. Next year the series will revert to three matches, with the addition of an ANZAC Day Bledisloe Test in Brisbane. It was a four-match series from 2020 and from 2008 to 2010, and a two-match series from 1999 into the early 2000s.

Commentator Tony Johnson noted that the holder currently needs to win only one Test to retain the Cup, which he said swings the series heavily in the holder's favour. The article proposes two options: a one-off Bledisloe Test alongside two Rugby Championship games, or putting the Cup on the line in every match, as with the Ranfurly Shield in New Zealand. The Cup also went missing for three decades after 1949 before being found in a Melbourne storeroom in 1979.
Rugby.copy:
In the 90 years since its inception, the Bledisloe Cup has – to borrow from the great US sitcom Veep – maintained one common thread: continuity with change. Curiously, New Zealand Rugby and Rugby Australia can’t agree on whether it was first played for in 1931 or 1932. Both unions agree that Lord Bledisloe, the New Zealand Governor-General from 1930 to 1935, donated the giant trophy early in his reign, and unsurprisingly, both contend it was first played for when they won.

But since 1931 or 1932, the format has changed a lot. For the last few years, it has been played as a two-Test series. Next year, with the addition of the ANZAC Day Bledisloe Test in Brisbane, it will revert to the three-match series it was mostly through the 2010s.

Rugby.title: 'Haven't been showing up': Ex-All Black and Jeremy Paul lay into Wallabies after Bledisloe defeats
Rugby.summary: Former Wallabies hooker Jeremy Paul chimed in, agreeing with Read, admitting he turned the game off late in the contest.
bullets: Former All Blacks loose forward Kieran Read has criticised the Wallabies' showing in the Bledisloe Cup, saying they lacked character and have not been showing up. Les Kiss's side had gone unbeaten in his first five games in charge, including a win over the Springboks in Perth, before losing at Eden Park and then in front of a crowd of more than 73,000 at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Rugby Podcast, Read said the Wallabies were mentally off despite a nation backing them, and that structure matters less than turning up. Former Wallabies hooker Jeremy Paul agreed, saying he turned the television off late in the game for the first time in over a decade.
Rugby.copy:
Former All Blacks loose-forward Kieran Read has made his feelings clear about the Wallabies’ recent performances in the Bledisloe Cup, where Les Kiss’ side failed to turn hope into reality.

The Wallabies turned up to Eden Park with confidence after going unbeaten through Kiss’ first five games in charge, including an impressive victory over the Springboks in Perth.

Rugby.title: WRU issue statement after passing of RGC player Jack Davies
Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union have joined the Welsh rugby community in mourning the loss of 24-year-old RGC player Jack Davies.
Rugby.copy:
The Welsh Rugby Union have joined the Welsh rugby community in mourning the loss of 24-year-old RGC player Jack Davies. Davies has been remembered as a valued member of the RGC and CR Caernarfon family, with all clubs involved in his rugby journey sharing heartfelt condolences after his sudden passing.

Davies earned his place in the RGC Pathway after shining for Clwb Rygbi Caernarfon at a young age. He returned to Caernarfon and RGC in 2023 after studying physical education at Cardiff Metropolitan University.

Rugby.title: The two players that could be Les Kiss’s silver bullet
Rugby.summary: These are two genuine impact players and difference makers the Wallabies can no longer afford to ignore.
bullets: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has said "the time we have is the time that we have" as his side build towards the 2027 Rugby World Cup, after a heavy defeat to the All Blacks in Sydney. The Wallabies made 17 linebreaks, one more than New Zealand, but averaged only 0.9m post-contact per carry against the All Blacks' 0.7m. Across 2026 they have averaged about 2.3m, compared with South Africa's 3.2m and the All Blacks' 2.8m.

The article argues that Samu Kerevi and Langi Gleeson could add the carrying power Kiss wants. Gleeson has been named on Kiss's 'unavailable list' in each of four squad announcements. In Super Rugby Pacific 2025 he made 2.4m post-contact per carry, scored seven tries and beat 33 defenders, against 1.9m, one try and 27 for Rob Valetini. Montpellier said on 10 September that Gleeson, who has a knee injury, should return in about two months, in time for the April Bledisloe.
Rugby.copy:
The Wallabies have shown glimpses of physical dominance, attacking brilliance, and defensive pressure in 2026, but are yet to string together an 80-minute performance. It is now clear that while coach Les Kiss has been chopping and changing the side in a bid to build genuine competition and depth in the squad, you can’t rush an exercise which takes time: time which the Wallabies don’t have.

In the wake of the Wallabies walloping in Sydney at the hands of the All Blacks, Kiss was asked about the clock ticking until the home Rugby World Cup in 2027. “The time we have is the time that we have,” Kiss said.

Rugby.title: SVNS great says Bledisloe II offered ‘taste’ of Rugby World Cup 2027
Rugby.summary: All Blacks Sevens great Karl Te Nana is confident Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 will be a massive hit in Australia.
bullets: More than 73,000 fans attended the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026 at Accor Stadium, the biggest Bledisloe crowd at the venue in 10 years. The All Blacks won 43-21, with Beauden Barrett and Josh Moorby scoring two tries each. All Blacks Sevens great Karl Te Nana said the atmosphere offered a taste of Men's Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia.

The stadium will host two quarter-finals, both semi-finals, the bronze final and the final at the 2027 tournament, as well as Australia v New Zealand in the pool stage 357 days after Bledisloe II. World Rugby says 1.3 million tickets have been bought by fans from 164 countries. The tournament, which opens on 1 October 2027, will have 24 teams and 52 matches across seven host cities, with about 250,000 overseas visitors reportedly expected.
Rugby.copy:
All Blacks Sevens great Karl Te Nana is confident Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 will be a massive hit in Australia, after more than 73,000 fans packed the stands at Accor Stadium for the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026.

Beauden Barrett and Josh Moorby scored two tries each as the All Blacks ran away with a 43-21 win at the Sydney venue, which will host two quarter-finals, both semi-finals, the bronze final and the Rugby World Cup Final at next year’s event.

Rugby.title: All Blacks take another step towards solving second-row puzzle
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' second-row depth has been the cause of a persistent selection headache in 2026, but a stand-out performance in Sydney's second Bledisloe Test has left forwards coach Jason Ryan with nothing but praise for his starting duo.
bullets: All Blacks forwards coach Jason Ryan has praised the starting second-row pairing of Fabian Holland and Scott Barrett after the second Bledisloe Test in Sydney. Both missed the entire 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season through injury, Holland with a shoulder problem sustained in a pre-season game and Barrett with back trouble after returning from a sabbatical in May. Ryan said the starting front row and two locks were "massive" in the win.

Ryan said Holland was coming back into form after shoulder reconstruction, and that Barrett's return was a reward for his rehabilitation, with the World Cup under 12 months away. He also said the scrum operated at 100 per cent across the two-Test series. Ryan added that ball-in-play time was probably the biggest ever, which means the bench needs careful management.
Rugby.copy:
The All Blacks‘ second-row depth has been the cause of a persistent selection headache in 2026, but a stand-out performance in Sydney’s second Bledisloe Test has left forwards coach Jason Ryan with nothing but praise for his starting duo.

Both Fabian Holland and Scott Barrett missed the entire 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season due to injuries, with Holland sustaining a shoulder injury in a pre-season hit-out and Barrett running into back trouble as he looked to return from a non-playing sabbatical in May.

Rugby.title: HKCR MEN'S SEVEN SWEEP ASIA RUGBY SEVENS SERIES; WOMEN TAKE BRONZE
Rugby.summary: HKCR MEN'S SEVEN SWEEP ASIA RUGBY SEVENS SERIES; WOMEN TAKE BRONZE Hong Kong China Rugby
bullets: Hong Kong China Rugby's men won the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series on 19 October, despite losing the Colombo cup final 28-14 to Japan. Hong Kong had won the opening leg in Suzhou, China, and reached both finals, earning a sixth straight Asian Sevens title on top of a third straight Asian Games gold earlier this month.

The women finished third overall in Asia, beating Kazakhstan 17-5 in the Colombo third-place match after a 17-7 semi-final loss to China. Nam Ka Man played her 50th tournament in Sri Lanka. Men's coach Jevon Groves said fatigue after the Asian Games was a factor, and the team will have a week off before preparing for the challenger event.
Rugby.copy:
[Hong Kong China, 19 October 2026]: Hong Kong China Rugby’s sevens athletes have concluded a successful Asian swing with the men sweeping the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series today in Sri Lanka, while the women finished third overall in Asia as they maintained their momentum from the Asian Games.

The men suffered a rare loss in the cup final in Colombo, being well beaten by Japan, 28-14. Japan blitzed Hong Kong with two tries in the final two minutes of the first half and then opened the second with a quick score to lead 21-0 with three minutes remaining. A try from Max Denmark closed the gap to 21-7, but Japan replied quickly to push the lead out to 28-7 before Matt Worley scored late to close the gap to 28-14.

Rugby.title: How have Canada closed gap to world champions England?
Rugby.summary: Forty-one matches, four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but England's unbeaten run is over. So how did Canada close the gap to the Red Roses?
bullets: England's 41-match unbeaten run, which lasted nearly four years since 2022, ended with a 24-21 defeat by Canada in Toronto on Friday in front of a record home crowd of 18,621. It followed a 26-26 draw at Exeter's Sandy Park in September; before this autumn England had won all seven meetings between the sides this decade by an average margin of nearly 22 points.

Hooker Amy Cokayne said England were not "a million miles away" and that nothing needs to change massively. Canada head coach Kevin Rouet and many of his players have gained experience in England's PWR, and newer talents such as number eight Lizzie Gibson have emerged. England are without captain Zoe Stratford, Abbie Ward, Rosie Galligan and Marlie Packer, while Abby Dow has retired. The teams meet again on Friday in Ottawa.
Rugby.copy:
Forty-one matches, nearly four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but the Red Roses' unbeaten streak is over. It fell to the experienced Amy Cokayne to face the press this week after England lost their first match since 2022 against Canada.

"You can't dwell on it," said the Sale hooker, who has 95 international caps. "We weren't a million miles away, so it's not like we have to completely throw the book out - nothing needs to massively change to the way we play."

Rugby.title: Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup?
Rugby.summary: Wales boast a world-class scrum-half in Tomos Williams but Steve Tandy might have to assess his back-up before the 2027 World Cup.
bullets: Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams has started every Test he has been available for since Steve Tandy took charge in summer 2025, playing past the hour in every outing. He played 378 minutes in the 2026 Six Nations, compared with 357 for France's Antoine Dupont, 323 for Ireland's Jamison Gibson-Park and 302 for Scotland's Ben White.

Williams has shared matchday squads with only two other scrum-halves, Kieran Hardy and Reuben Morgan-Williams, and Hardy faces a lengthy lay-off with a knee injury. Dragons' Che Hope, 23, is among the options, though Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod urged caution. Gareth Davies, who retired from Test rugby in 2024 with 77 caps, has also been suggested as an emergency option. Wales open the 2027 World Cup against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October.
Rugby.copy:
There are few, if any, players more secure of a starting spot at next year's World Cup in Australia than Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams. France superstar Antoine Dupont has a rival for the nine jersey in Maxime Lucu, a talisman for back-to-back European champions Bordeaux-Begles.

Malcolm Marx, World Rugby player of the year, fights hard for his start as South Africa's hooker but must also be prepared for 'bomb squad' duty from the bench. The best players on the planet usually have a rival pushing them hard, but there is a gulf between 2025 British and Irish Lions tourist Williams and his fellow Welsh nines.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly: Prem clubs struggle in Europe
Rugby.summary: Danny, Ashy and Chris look back on round one of the Champions Cup.
Rugby.copy: Danny, Ashy and Chris reflect on a sombre opening weekend of the Champions Cup following the death of Lions and former Sale lock Hyron Andrews. They assess a chastening start for the Prem, with only one win from eight matches. Is it evidence of English rugby falling behind, or just a difficult opening weekend? Glasgow impress in the north west, Connacht turn on the style and Bath lose again. The Red Roses 41-match unbeaten run is over, but will the defeat to Canada prove to be a blessing in disguise? The All Blacks extend their winning run to 13 over the Wallabies and Spain enter the race to host the 2035 World Cup. Rugby in the Nou Camp anyone?

Rugby.title: Newcastle Red Bulls: Sale game is 'battle of North' even though Sharks 'really' midlands
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland says his side has their sights set on breaking their duck for the season and becoming Kings of the North by beating Sale Sharks on Friday night.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland says his side are aiming to secure their first win of the Gallagher PREM season against Sale Sharks on Friday night. Newcastle and Harlequins are the only winless teams, and four bonus points from the opening three games keep Newcastle off the foot of the table, five points behind seventh-placed Sale.

McFarland described the fixture as a "battle for the North", even though he said Sale are really in Cheshire, "sort of the Midlands". He acknowledged Sale have held primacy in recent years and have recruited well. Newcastle won 45-42 in May after recovering from 35-10 down, only their second win since 2 January. McFarland said the team is starting at the back of the grid but wants to pick off those ahead.
Rugby.copy:
Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland says his side has their sights set on breaking their duck for the season and becoming Kings of the North by beating Sale Sharks on Friday night.

The Red Bulls and Harlequins are the only two teams in the Gallagher PREM without a win this season, and the four bonus points they took in the opening three games are keeping them off the foot of the table.

Rugby.title: Nomadic Tommaso Allan has his sights set on playing in Australia next year
Rugby.summary: At 33, the utility back is intent on enjoying whatever the future holds.
bullets: Italy utility back Tommaso Allan, 33, has returned to his homeland by signing for Zebre Parma in the BKT URC, hoping the move will help him reach a fourth World Cup in Australia in just under a year. He has 91 caps and 552 points for Italy, making him the country's highest points scorer in both the Six Nations and the World Cup.

Born in Vicenza, Allan moved to England aged eight and played for Henley RFC and the Wasps Academy before joining Western Province in South Africa. He later played for Perpignan, Benetton and Harlequins, then returned to Perpignan before joining Zebre this summer. He has played at 10 and 15 for Zebre, whose next game is at Connacht on Friday. Allan said he is unsure how many years he has left but is enjoying a leadership role.
Rugby.copy:
After more than a decade of rugby wandering, Tommaso Allan is back in his homeland and determined to make the most of however long he has left in his career. Over the years, he has had spells playing in South Africa, France and England, as well as in his native Italy, while his 91 caps for the Azzurri have taken him around the world.

Now he has returned to the country of his birth by signing for Zebre Parma which means yet more border-hopping through being part of the multi-nation BKT URC. He is hoping the move will help him achieve his dream of playing in a fourth World Cup with a trip to Australia on the horizon in just under a year’s time.

Rugby.title: Leinster issue worrying injury update on Ireland No.8 Jack Conan
Rugby.summary: Leinster have confirmed that Ireland international Jack Conan has suffered a shoulder injury, casting fresh doubt over the province's back-row resources after Caelan Doris was already ruled out with a long-term foot and knee issue.
bullets: Leinster have confirmed that Ireland and British & Irish Lions No.8 Jack Conan suffered a shoulder injury in their 48-23 Investec Champions Cup Round 1 win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin. He was hurt while scoring a second-half try, and the province said he needs further assessment without giving a timeframe.

Caelan Doris is already out with a long-term foot and knee issue, leaving Leinster short in the back row. Jordan Larmour needs further assessment on a calf problem, and Hugh Cooney suffered a hand injury in the A game against Edinburgh. Leinster came back from 16-15 down at half-time by scoring 33 second-half points to secure a bonus-point win, and face Munster in the URC at the Aviva Stadium this weekend.
Rugby.copy:
Leinster have confirmed that Ireland international Jack Conan has suffered a shoulder injury, casting fresh doubt over the province’s back-row resources after Caelan Doris was already ruled out with a long-term foot and knee issue.

Conan was injured while scoring a crucial second-half try during Leinster’s impressive 48-23 Investec Champions Cup Round 1 victory over Clermont ASM at Stade Marcel-Michelin.

Rugby.title: SOS recruit: Exeter 'can't say that everything's signed, sealed, and delivered'
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has confirmed interest in signing Pumas lock André Goedhals to strengthen his injury-hit second row, but says the deal is far from done.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has confirmed interest in signing Pumas lock André Goedhals, 21, to cover for Italian lock Andrea Zambonin, who faces a lengthy absence after a shoulder operation. Goedhals was born in Devon and holds a British passport, making him English-qualified. Baxter said the deal is not yet "signed, sealed, and delivered".

Goedhals grew up in Riversdale in the Western Cape, won Springbok under-20 honours and moved to the Pumas from the Stormers set-up. He was part of the Pumas side that lost the Currie Cup final 23-16 to the Griquas in Kimberley last month. Baxter said Exeter are waiting on the Pumas to complete the proper process in South Africa and that pushing it through quicker would be disrespectful.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has confirmed interest in signing Pumas lock André Goedhals to strengthen his injury-hit second row, but says the deal is far from done. Baxter says he has been looking to bring someone into his Sandy Park outfit since learning in the summer that Italian star Andrea Zambonin faced a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a shoulder operation.

He has also spoken with the Currie Cup franchise about a move for Goedhals, who holds a British passport after being born in Devon while his parents lived and worked in England, making him English-qualified.

Rugby.title: Nations Championship: November rugby returns to RugbyPass TV
Rugby.summary: On Friday 6 November, the inaugural Nations Championship returns with three consecutive rounds of fixtures that will determine who faces off for continental supremacy.
bullets: The inaugural Nations Championship resumes on Friday 6 November with three further rounds. France top the Northern Hemisphere table on twelve points, while South Africa lead New Zealand on points difference in the south. The Springboks scored the most points (130) and tries (20) in the opening rounds, and the two hemispheres are level with nine wins each.

Round 4 includes Ireland v Argentina at the Aviva Stadium, Scotland v New Zealand, and England v Australia at Twickenham. Round 5 features France v South Africa in Paris. The regular stage ends on 21 November with England v New Zealand, Ireland v South Africa and Fiji v Italy. Finals Weekend runs from 27 to 29 November, with all twelve nations playing and the title decider at 16:40 UTC on the final day.
Rugby.copy:
On Friday 6 November, the inaugural Nations Championship returns with three consecutive rounds of fixtures that will determine who faces off for continental supremacy. Heading into the home stretch, France sit top of the Northern Hemisphere table with twelve points, while back-to-back Rugby World Cup champions South Africa are ahead of the All Blacks on points difference on the Southern Hemisphere side.

With three more weeks of action to look forward to, RugbyPass looks back on the major takeaways from the opening rounds of the tournament and previews what’s to come. Unsurprisingly, Southern Hemisphere heavyweights New Zealand and South Africa put down early markers on home soil. The Springboks scored the most points (130) and the most tries (20) as they swept to three home victories. Their aerial dominance, set piece ability, and electric wingers proved too much for the opposition and will take some stopping if anyone hopes to rein in the world champions.

Rugby.title: Ex-Scotland captain Ritchie set for Glasgow debut
Rugby.summary: Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut this weekend.
bullets: Former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie is expected to make his Glasgow Warriors debut in Saturday's United Rugby Championship match against Benetton in Treviso. The 30-year-old flanker, capped 63 times, joined from French club Perpignan in the summer on a two-year deal. He has missed the start of the season with ankle and Achilles tendon problems and is now back in full training.

Assistant coach Nigel Carolan said the club had not wanted to rush Ritchie after summer surgery and a move to a new club. He said he would like Ritchie involved either starting or on the bench, ahead of Scotland's Nations Cup in a couple of weeks. Glasgow are second in the URC after three matches, behind Edinburgh, and face second-bottom Benetton.
Rugby.copy:
Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut. The former Edinburgh flanker signed from French club Perpignan in the summer but has been sidelined for the opening months of the season because of ankle and Achilles tendon issues.

The 30-year-old, capped 63 times, is now back in full training and is expected to play in Saturday's United Rugby Championship (URC) match against Benetton in Treviso. "He's training fully. We feel he's integrated into the systems now very well. And he's itching to go," said Carolan.

Rugby.title: Pat Lam explains sending Bristol Bears B team to Cape Town after Stormers hammering
Rugby.summary: Pat Lam, the Bristol Bears Director of Rugby, was candid in his assessment of the team's opening stanza of the season.
bullets: Bristol Bears Director of Rugby Pat Lam explained his decision to send the youngest and most inexperienced side he has selected to Cape Town for the Champions Cup opener, which Bristol lost 49-12 to the Stormers after leading 21-12 at one stage. Ellis Genge (injured), Louis Rees-Zammit, Fitz Harding and AJ MacGinty did not travel, and hooker Gabriel Oghre missed out with a calf strain.

Lam said the Champions Cup opening round was brought forward from December into October, and that the short turnaround before the Exeter match meant workloads had to be managed. He described it as probably Bristol's toughest first six games up to November and said no player can play six games in a row. He added that the young players, several from the Academy and most due to feature in the November Premiership Cup, would benefit from the experience.
Rugby.copy:
Pat Lam, the Bristol Bears Director of Rugby, was candid in his assessment of the team’s opening stanza of the season. As the only Premiership team to travel to South Africa and play a red-hot Stormers outfit in Cape Town in the opening round of the Champions Cup, Lam opted to prioritise the domestic league over Europe.

The trip to the Republic is sandwiched between Premiership encounters with Sale Sharks (an impressive 34-24 away win), Northampton Saints (a 41-26 win at home), an way loss to Saracens (7-30), along with two vital home fixtures against Exeter and Leicester Tigers.

Rugby.title: All Blacks have Springboks within their sights in World Rankings
Rugby.summary: Resounding back-to-back Bledisloe Cup wins have put the All Blacks within touching distance of the Springboks again at the top of the World Rugby Men's Rankings.
bullets: Back-to-back Bledisloe Cup wins of 50-19 in Auckland and 43-21 in Sydney have narrowed the gap between the All Blacks and the Springboks in the World Rugby Men's Rankings to 0.82 points. South Africa are on 93.09 and New Zealand on 92.27. Nearly four points separated the sides when the Springboks won the series 3-1 in Baltimore in mid-September.

The Springboks lost to the Wallabies later that month, and they cannot improve their rankings score when the Nations Championship resumes on 7 November because they face an Italian team outside the world's top 10. New Zealand could close the gap further by beating Scotland, who have never beaten the All Blacks. Scotland have moved above Australia into sixth place, with the Wallabies dropping to seventh after losing 0.46 points.
Rugby.copy:
Resounding back-to-back Bledisloe Cup wins have put the All Blacks within touching distance of the Springboks again at the top of the World Rugby Men’s Rankings. The 50-19 and 43-21 victories in Auckland and Sydney have closed the gap between rugby’s so-called greatest rivals to just 0.82 points, with the Springboks sitting on 93.09 points to New Zealand’s 92.27.

Nearly four points separated the teams when the Springboks wrapped up a 3-1 series win over the All Blacks in Baltimore in mid-September, but their defeat to the Wallabies later in the month, and New Zealand’s dominant Bledisloe Cup campaign has changed the picture.

Rugby.title: Wales great Evans to leave role as Lions chairman
Rugby.summary: British and Irish Lions are looking for a new chair as former Wales captain Ieuan Evans' term comes to an end after almost four years.
bullets: Ieuan Evans will stand down as chair of the British and Irish Lions on Wednesday after almost four years in the role. The former Wales captain was appointed in 2022 and is coming to the end of his term. He was tour manager last year when the men's team beat Australia in a series under Andy Farrell.

The Lions have begun searching for a new chair ahead of next year's inaugural women's tour to New Zealand. Evans, 62, said he was proud of the 2025 tour's success and of progress towards the first women's tour. He oversaw governance changes that brought independent directors onto the board. Chief executive Ben Calveley praised his passion for the Lions and understanding of the organisation.
Rugby.copy:
Ieuan Evans will stand down as chair of the British and Irish Lions on Wednesday after almost four years in the role. The former Wales captain, who played on tours to Australia in 1989, New Zealand in 1993 and South Africa in 1997, was appointed in 2022 and is coming to the end of his term.

Ex-wing Evans was tour manager last year when the men's team recorded a series victory against the Wallabies under Andy Farrell. The Lions have started the search for a new chair before next year's inaugural women's tour to New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Northampton 'security incident' believed to be a hoax
Rugby.summary: Police are investigating the incident at Saints' Franklin's Gardens "following threats made on social media".
bullets: A security incident during Northampton's 28-12 Champions Cup win over Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens on Sunday is believed to have been a hoax. Police were called to the stadium at about 19:00 BST following threats made on social media. The match had kicked off at 17:30, and players from both sides left the field straight after the final whistle as a precaution.

Northamptonshire Police said enquiries remain ongoing and that they are working closely with the club and policing partners. Northampton said they were sorry supporters did not get to see the players after the final whistle. The club added that the safety of supporters, players, staff and officials will always be its top priority.
Rugby.copy:
A 'security incident' during Northampton's Champions Cup win over Cardiff on Sunday is believed to have been a hoax. Police were called to the Saints' Franklin's Gardens stadium at about 19:00 BST "following threats made on social media".
