New Zealand’s 23 linebreaks dwarfed France’s tally of two, and while Ayesha Leti-I’iga was responsible for four of them, there were 11 other Kiwis who broke the French line in a superb team performance. 20-year-old rookie Shyrah Tuliau-Tua’a bagged four second-half tries while Amy Du Plessis, Maia Joseph and Ayesha Leti-I’iga all scored doubles.

Rugby.title: Black Ferns player ratings vs France in Hamilton | WXV Global Series 2026
Rugby.summary: It took just 67 seconds for New Zealand to get their first five points on the board on a sunny afternoon in Hamilton, and those 67 seconds were as close as France would get in the opening Test of this three-game series.
bullets: New Zealand scored their first try after 67 seconds and led 43-0 at half-time before winning 81-12 against France in Hamilton in the opening Test of the series. Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a scored four tries in her fourth Test and second start. Olsen-Baker led the Test in metres carried, and the Black Ferns made 14 first-half linebreaks.

Head coach Whitney Hansen said the challenge is now to repeat the effort against a France side desperate for a more respectable scoreline in the second Test. The Black Ferns' lineout operated at 91 per cent against France's 50 per cent, and they had 62 per cent possession. Tests in Whangarei and Christchurch remain.
Rugby.copy:
It took just 67 seconds for New Zealand to get their first five points on the board on a sunny afternoon in Hamilton, and those 67 seconds were as close as France would get in the opening Test of this three-game series.

It was 43-0 by halftime, and 81-12 by full-time. The Kiwis have set an impressive marker with Tests in Whangarei and Christchurch remaining in the series. Head coach Whitney Hansen says the challenge is now to repeat the effort against a France side who will be desperate to at least earn a more respectable scoreline in game 2.

Rugby.title: Maddison Levi stars as Australia claim pre-SVNS bragging rights against NZ
Rugby.summary: HSBC SVNS Series phenom Maddison Levi scored seven tries as Australia finished with a 2-1 record against arch-rivals New Zealand.
bullets: Maddison Levi scored seven tries in three games as Australia's women's sevens side won the series 2-1 against New Zealand in Sydney. Australia won both Kick On 7s matches on Friday, 24-19 and 36-26, before the Black Ferns Sevens won 21-12 on Saturday. Levi scored five tries on Friday, including a hat-trick in the second match.

Jorja Miller led New Zealand's response on Saturday, with Jazmin Felix-Hotham and Renee Holmes also scoring. Australia captain Isabella Nasser said the wins set up confidence for Dubai in a couple of months. In the men's matches, Australia and Fiji drew the series, with Australia winning 24-14, Fiji winning 10-0 and the final match ending 19-19.
Rugby.copy:
HSBC SVNS Series phenom Maddison Levi scored seven tries in three games as Australia finished with a 2-1 record against arch-rivals New Zealand. The Black Ferns Sevens avoided a series sweep with a 21-12 win on a picture-perfect Saturday afternoon in Sydney.

Australia prevailed in the two Kick On 7s matches on Friday evening, with the reigning HSBC SVNS World Championship winners making a bit of a statement in pre-season. But Jorja Miller led the way as the New Zealanders bounced back in style.

Rugby.title: Late charge from Canada ends England’s 41-match unbeaten run
Rugby.summary: .England were stunned by a late rally from Canada as the Red Roses fell 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto.
bullets: Canada beat England 24-21 in the WXV Global Series in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run. Replacement Shoshanah Seumanutafa scored the winning try in the 77th minute. England led 14-5 at half-time through tries from Maddie Feaunati and Zoe Harrison, after Savannah Bauder had opened the scoring for Canada in the 15th minute.

DaLeaka Menin's 63rd-minute try kept Canada in contention before Seumanutafa's score. England head coach John Mitchell said the team were disappointed by the result but saw positives, and that the loss frees them up to find more. England face Canada again next Saturday in Ottawa, then the USA in New Jersey on 30 October.
Rugby.copy:
England were stunned by a late rally from Canada as the Red Roses fell 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto. Shoshanah Seumanutafa came off the bench to score the match-winning try in the 77th minute, bringing England’s 41-match unbeaten run to an end.

Following a draw in their previous clash last month in Exeter, Canada looked up for the challenge early as they opened the scoring through Savannah Bauder in the 15th minute. Quickfire tries to Maddie Feaunati and Zoe Harrison just before half-time put England ahead 14-5 at the break.

Rugby.title: Talking points as Canada end England's 41-match unbeaten streak in Toronto
Rugby.summary: Shoshanah Seumanutafa’s 77th-minute try ended England's 41-match unbeaten run as Canada beat the world champions 24-21 at Toronto's BMO Field.
bullets: Shoshanah Seumanutafa's 77th-minute try gave Canada a 24-21 win over England at Toronto's BMO Field, ending England's 41-match unbeaten run. A crowd of 18,621 set a record for a standalone women's rugby fixture in North America and was the largest for a Canadian Test in over a decade. Sophie de Goede made 20 tackles and kicked conversions.

Canada made 165 tackles to England's 218, and the match resembled the 26-26 draw at Sandy Park three weeks earlier. England face Canada again in Ottawa next week, with defence coach Shaun Edwards in camp. Canada and the USA end their calendar years against each other at Sports Illustrated Stadium on Friday, 30 October.
Rugby.copy:
Shoshanah Seumanutafa’s 77th-minute try ended England’s 41-match unbeaten run as Canada beat the world champions 24-21 at Toronto’s BMO Field. It was an enthralling 80 minutes on the banks of Lake Ontario as the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 finalists met for the second time in a month.

A total of 18,621 supporters made their way to BMO Field for the WXV Global Series game, setting a new attendance record for a standalone women’s rugby fixture in North America. It was also the largest attendance for a Canadian Test match in over a decade.

Rugby.title: Suite Spot: 48 Hours in Hong Kong for the Rugby Sevens
Rugby.summary: Suite Spot: 48 Hours in Hong Kong for the Rugby Sevens Man of Many
Rugby.copy:
Some trips live up to the hype. Others go well beyond it. I’d been wanting to experience Hong Kong’s Rugby Sevens for years, having heard the stories from friends who’d made the pilgrimage. The rugby, the costumes, the parties in the South Stand. It sounded like one of those events you simply had to experience.

Earlier this year, I finally got my chance, heading to Hong Kong for the tournament’s 50th anniversary. What followed was a weekend of ridiculously good rugby, excellent food, world-class bars and a city that has something happening around every corner. Here’s how I spent 48 hours in Hong Kong…
Rugby.skip_reason: travel lifestyle piece, not sports news

Rugby.title: Wallaroos vs Scotland takes: X-factor at No. 9, Aussies put on a show
Rugby.summary: The Wallaroos have run away with an emphatic WXV Global Series win over Scotland, giving Sydney fans plenty to cheer about.
bullets: The Wallaroos beat Scotland 56-12 in the WXV Global Series at Accor Stadium in Sydney. Scotland scored first through Katie Buchanan in the fourth minute, but Australia led by 30 at half-time after five tries to one. Amelia Whitaker and Desiree Miller each scored twice, and Brittany Merlo, Maya Stewart and Waiaria Ellis also scored. Eva Karpani scored in the final minute on her 49th Test appearance.

Australia also won by 20 points in Edinburgh late last month, the first of three straight meetings with the Scots. Scrum-half Samantha Wood, 22, directed play and kicked goals. Scotland's Evie Gallagher made 17 tackles with no misses by the 50-minute mark. Scotland had 42 per cent possession. This was the Wallaroos' second-last Test of the season.
Rugby.copy:
Wallaroos vs Scotland takes: X-factor at No. 9, Aussies put on a show The Wallaroos have run away with an emphatic 56-12 WXV Global Series win over Scotland, giving Sydney fans plenty to cheer about on a picture-perfect afternoon in the Harbour City.

Australia claimed a 20-point win over the same opposition in Edinburgh late last month, in the first of three straight meetings with the Scots. Scotland actually struck first at Accor Stadium, with Katie Buchanan quickly changing direction during a rapid burst to the try line in the fourth minute.

Rugby.title: Late Canada fightback ends Red Roses' unbeaten streak
Rugby.summary: Canada fight back to beat England 24-21 in Toronto in the WXV Global Series, with Shoshanah Seumanutafa's 77th-minute try ending the Red Roses' unbeaten run, stretching back to the 2022 Rugby World Cup final.

Rugby.title: Gloucester earn thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux in Champions Cup opener
Rugby.summary: Gloucester 36-36 Bordeaux : Will Trenholm bagged a brace but it wasn’t enough for George Skivington’s team to down last season’s champions
bullets: Gloucester drew 36-36 with Champions Cup holders Bordeaux in their opening tie at Kingsholm Stadium. Will Trenholm scored twice for the hosts after they led 24-17 at half-time, while Louis Bielle-Biarrey also crossed twice for Bordeaux and levelled the scores in the 62nd minute.

Bordeaux scored first through Martin Page-Relo in the fourth minute, and Arthur Clark replied immediately for Gloucester. Max Llewellyn, George Barton and Sipili Falatea also scored before the break, with Barton kicking three conversions. In the Challenge Cup, Dragons beat Perpignan 29-14 at Rodney Parade, and Edinburgh lost 27-17 to Toulon, for whom Malvyn Jaminet scored 22 points.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. A brace by Will Trenholm was not enough to prevent Gloucester falling agonisingly short of downing Champions Cup holders Bordeaux following a thrilling 36-36 draw.

George Skivington’s team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium. Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux.

Rugby.title: Four-try Dragons beat Perpignan
Rugby.summary: Dragons turn a half-time deficit around to beat Perpignan in their Challenge Cup opener at Rodney Parade.
bullets: Dragons began their Challenge Cup campaign with a win over Perpignan at Rodney Parade, scoring four tries through Jared Rosser, Aneurin Owen, Anzelo Tuitavuki and Fetuli Paea. They did not earn a bonus point because this season's rule change requires five tries when the opposition score twice. Perpignan led 7-5 at the break after Jules Coulon's try, and Posolo Tuilagi also scored for them.

Dragons, semi-finalists in 2025-26, were without several influential players ahead of a derby at Ospreys. They face the Cheetahs at St Helen's in Swansea in December, then Bayonne in Newport and Ulster in Belfast in January. Loose-head props Rhodri and Wyn Jones went off injured, a week after Rodrigo Martinez was injured in defeat by Ospreys.
Rugby.copy:
Dragons started their Challenge Cup campaign with a hard-fought win against Perpignan at Rodney Parade. Filo Tiatia's side, semi-finalists in 2025-26, ran in four tries in Newport to edge a scrappy opener, but did not claim a bonus point after this season's change in rules.

Perpignan led 7-5 after a drab first half by responding to Jared Rosser's opener with a try from Jules Coulon. Dragons backs Aneurin Owen and Anzelo Tuitavuki scored either side of a powerful effort by Posolo Tuilagi to secure victory against their French opponents, with Fetuli Paea adding a flourish in the closing stages.

Rugby.title: Jaminet stars as Toulon beat Edinburgh in Challenge Cup
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh suffer their first defeat of the season as they go down to Toulon in their European Challenge Cup opener.
bullets: Toulon beat Edinburgh in their European Challenge Cup opener, handing Edinburgh their first defeat of the season. Full-back Melvyn Jaminet scored two tries and contributed 22 points, including two penalties, the second from well inside his own half, to give Toulon a 6-0 lead before James Grayson's penalty cut the gap to three points at the break.

Jaminet scored early in the second half after a turnover, and Edinburgh hit back through Ewan Ashman from a set-piece. Seta Tuicuvu then scored from a maul to make it 20-10, and Geordie Gwynn's try after Tom Currie's tackle brought Edinburgh back into contention. Jaminet's second try, set up by Jeremy Sinzelle after another rolling maul, all but ended Edinburgh's resistance.
Rugby.copy:
Edinburgh suffered their first defeat of the season as they went down to Toulon in their European Challenge Cup opener. Melvyn Jaminet inspired the French side to victory, scoring two tries and contributing 22 points in a superb individual display.

The France full-back kicked two penalties, the second from well inside his own half, to give the visitors a 6-0 lead. Edinburgh engineered some good openings but were unable to break through as they were met with some fierce French goal-line defence.

Rugby.title: Gloucester and holders Bordeaux draw Champions Cup thriller
Rugby.summary: Gloucester and holders Bordeaux Begles begin this season's Champions Cup with a thrilling 36-36 draw at Kingsholm.
bullets: Gloucester and holders Bordeaux Begles drew 36-36 at Kingsholm in their opening Champions Cup Pool Three match. Bordeaux, seeking a third successive title, trailed 24-17 at half-time and 36-29 after replacement Will Trenholm scored twice for Gloucester, but Louis Bielle-Biarrey's second try, converted by Maxime Lucu, levelled the scores.

Both sides scored five tries and had chances late on: Gloucester kicked a penalty to touch instead of going for goal and lost possession, while Bordeaux failed to capitalise on a late scrum in Gloucester territory. Before kick-off there was a moment's silence for Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday aged 31. Gloucester's first-half tries owed much to their scrummaging strength.
Rugby.copy:
Gloucester and holders Bordeaux Begles began this season's Champions Cup with a thrilling 36-36 draw at Kingsholm. Bordeaux, bidding to win the Champions Cup for a third successive year, had looked in danger of their first loss in the competition since a quarter-final defeat by Harlequins in April 2024.

The French side trailed 24-17 at the interval and then 36-29 when Gloucester replacement Will Trenholm crossed twice midway through the second half for the early-season Prem leaders.

Rugby.title: South African rugby player dies on tour after fall at team hotel
Rugby.summary: The sport has paid tribute to Hyron Andrews, a lock forward for the Lions, who was in France on club duty for the Champions Cup and previously played for his country at Under-20 level, while featuring in the Prem for Sale Sharks
bullets: Hyron Andrews, the 31-year-old Lions lock, has died after a fall at the team's hotel in La Rochelle during a tour to France. He previously played for the Sharks and made 45 appearances for Sale Sharks in England, and he had recently joined the Lions this season. He leaves behind his wife and two young sons.

The Lions will still play their Champions Cup match against Stade Rochelais on Saturday in honour of their teammate. A moment's silence will be held before every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend, and Sale will pay tribute before their game against Glasgow Warriors. SA Rugby president Mark Alexander and Lions chief executive Rudolf Straeuli were among those to pay tribute.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. South Africa Rugby has paid tribute to “gifted” Hyron Andrews after the Lions lock forward’s tragic death after falling at the team’s hotel during a tour to France.

The 31-year-old, who played for KZN Sharks and Sale Sharks in England, has passed away following an accident at the team’s hotel in La Rochelle. Andrews leaves behind his wife, Maiglin, and young sons, with his Lions teammates set to play their European Champions Cup match against Stade Rochelais on Saturday.

Rugby.title: Moving match to Thomond for Foley tributes 'not practicable'
Rugby.summary: Munster Rugby defends the decision to play Saturday's European opener at Pairc Ui Chaoimh, amid criticism that tributes to Anthony Foley will be held away from Thomond Park.
bullets: Munster Rugby has defended its decision to play Saturday's Champions Cup opener against Racing 92 at Pairc Ui Chaoimh rather than Thomond Park, despite criticism from supporters, including former Munster fly-half and Racing 92 head coach Ronan O'Gara. The match, which kicks off at 20:00 BST, falls 10 years after head coach Anthony Foley died at the team hotel before a game against Racing 92 in Paris in October 2016.

Munster said the venue was set in March, before the July draw, and that neither Racing 92 nor the anniversary could have been anticipated, so a change was not considered practicable. Planned tributes, made with the support of Foley's family, include commemorative jackets bearing his number eight, applause in the eighth minute, a rendition of 'There Is An Isle' and a photo display in Marina Park outside the stadium.
Rugby.copy:
Munster Rugby has defended the decision to play Saturday's European opener at Pairc Ui Chaoimh amid criticism that tributes to Anthony Foley will be held away from Thomond Park.

Head coach and former player Foley died suddenly in his sleep aged 42 at the team hotel ahead of Munster's European game with Racing 92 in Paris in October 2016. The sides will meet again 10 years on in the opening round of the Investec Champions Cup on Saturday (20:00 BST), with tributes planned to remember Foley at the game at Pairc Ui Chaoimh.

Rugby.title: Former Sale Sharks lock Andrews dies at team hotel in La Rochelle
Rugby.summary: Hyron Andrews dies at his Johannesburg Lions' team hotel before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle on Saturday.
bullets: Former Sale Sharks lock Hyron Andrews has died aged 31 at the Johannesburg Lions' team hotel in La Rochelle, ahead of their Champions Cup match against La Rochelle. SA Rugby described his death as an accident after a fall, while local reports claim he suffered a heart attack in the shower. The public prosecutor in La Rochelle is investigating.

The Lions will play the fixture, which kicks off at 17:30 BST, in Andrews' honour, and a moment's silence will be observed at all the opening round's fixtures. Andrews joined Sale in February 2024 from the Sharks, made 45 appearances and left in the summer to return to South Africa. Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson said he was a brilliant team-mate and a devoted husband and father. His death comes 10 years after Munster coach Anthony Foley died before a Champions Cup match in Paris.
Rugby.copy:
Former Sale second row Hyron Andrews has died at his Johannesburg Lions' team hotel before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle on Saturday. A statement from SA Rugby stated that his death had been an "accident" and that the 31-year-old had "died after a fall".

The public prosecutor in La Rochelle is investigating, with local reports claiming Andrews suffered a heart attack while in the shower. "We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron," said Lions chief executive Rudolf Straeuli.

Rugby.title: Atkin-Davies returns to rugby after birth of daughter
Rugby.summary: England hooker Lark Atkin-Davies is to make her competitive playing return for Bristol Bears following the birth of her first child.
bullets: England hooker Lark Atkin-Davies is to make her competitive return for Bristol Bears after giving birth to her first child 16 weeks ago. The 31-year-old will start in the Bears' PWR Cup match against Harlequins on Saturday. Her last game was the World Cup final in September 2025, when she won the title with the Red Roses after playing in all six of their matches at the tournament.

Atkin-Davies joined Bristol in 2022 and follows Bears and England team-mate Abbie Ward in returning to the sport after having a baby. Lock Ward gave birth to her second child this summer, while England captain Zoe Stratford also had her first child in recent weeks. Bristol begin the 2026-27 Premiership Women's Rugby campaign away at Harlequins on Sunday, 22 November.
Rugby.copy:
England hooker Lark Atkin-Davies is to make her competitive playing return for Bristol Bears following the birth of her first child. Atkin-Davies welcomed her daughter 16 weeks ago and will start for the Bears in their PWR Cup match against Harlequins on Saturday.

The 31-year-old's last game was the World Cup final in September 2025, where she clinched the title with the Red Roses having played in all six of their matches during the tournament.

Rugby.title: Munster make 6 changes and retire No.8 jersey for Champions Cup opener
Rugby.summary: Munster will retire their No.8 jersey in honour of Anthony Foley when they launch their Investec Champions Cup campaign against Racing 92 at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh on Saturday night.
bullets: Munster will retire their No.8 jersey in honour of Anthony Foley when they open their Investec Champions Cup campaign against Racing 92 at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh on Saturday night. The week marks the 10th anniversary of Foley's death, with tributes and commemorative events planned around the fixture. The shirt was also retired for Munster's first match after his death in 2016.

Munster have made six changes to the side that drew with Ulster in Belfast last weekend, with four young players in line for Champions Cup debuts. First-year Academy fly-half Charlie O'Shea starts alongside Ireland's Craig Casey, flanker Seán Edogbo also starts, and replacements Max Clein and Ben O'Donovan could make debuts. Head coach Clayton McMillan said the players are determined to give a performance Foley would be proud of, and that the best way to honour him is a committed team display.
Rugby.copy:
Munster will retire their No.8 jersey in honour of Anthony Foley when they launch their Investec Champions Cup campaign against Racing 92 at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh on Saturday night.

This week marks the 10th anniversary of Foley’s death, with a series of tributes and commemorative events planned around the province’s opening European fixture. In a gesture reflecting the legendary back-rower’s enduring legacy, the No.8 shirt will once again be retired for the occasion, as was the case for Munster’s first match following his passing in 2016.

Rugby.title: England U18 Women name 67-Player squad for first camp of the season
Rugby.summary: The England Under-18 Women's programme will start with a four-day camp at the University of Nottingham.
bullets: The England Under-18 Women's programme begins its season with a four-day camp at the University of Nottingham, running from Friday 16 October to Monday 19 October. A total of 67 players will take part, split into forwards and backs, for positional meetings, on-field training, unit meetings, strength and conditioning work and educational workshops.

All nine of the RFU's Player Development Group sites are represented in the squad, which was named shortly after regional training earlier in October. Fourteen players are previously capped at U18 level, including Holly Bagnowiec, Zara Barringer and Charlie Williams. The group will regather in December for a three-day camp at Bisham Abbey National Sports Centre. Head coach James Cooper said the opening camp is a chance for players to showcase their abilities and embrace the standards of the England pathway.
Rugby.copy:
The England Under-18 Women’s programme will start with a four-day camp at the University of Nottingham. Starting on Friday 16 October and concluding on Monday 19 October, 67 players will take part in the camp. Split into forwards and backs, the group will take part in positional meetings, on-field training sessions, unit meetings, strength and conditioning work and educational workshops.

All nine of the RFU’s Player Development Group sites are included in the squad – which has been named shortly after regional training earlier in October. Holly Bagnowiec, Zara Barringer, Scarlett Beech, Rosalyn Civil, Alice Fleming, Hannah Foley, Beth Hall, Mali Hill, Christal Koroiyadi, Eva Larkai, Isabella Lyndon, Maisie Trotman, Rowan Turney and Charlie Williams are all previously capped at U18 level.

Rugby.title: Struggling Harlequins get Los Pumas star back as 1 of 4 changes for Vannes
Rugby.summary: Harlequins have welcomed back Argentina international Rodrigo Isgró as one of four changes to their starting XV for Sunday's EPCR Challenge Cup opener against RC Vannes at The Stoop.
bullets: Harlequins have made four changes for Sunday's EPCR Challenge Cup opener against RC Vannes at The Stoop, with Argentina wing Rodrigo Isgró returning on the right flank. Head coach Jason Gilmore is looking to improve the Gallagher PREM side's season after a challenging start to the domestic campaign. Isgró joins captain Cadan Murley and full-back George Furbank in the back three, while Marcus Smith continues at fly-half alongside scrum-half Lucas Friday.

Former European champion Guido Petti Pagadizábal comes in at blindside flanker, and the front row is unchanged, with hooker Sam Riley having scored twice in last week's defeat to Sale Sharks. England Under-20 hooker Jimmy Staples is on the bench and in line for his European debut. Gilmore has again opted for a six-two bench split, and Elliot Williams is named in a senior matchday squad for the first time since pre-season.
Rugby.copy:
PREM strugglers Harlequins have welcomed back Argentina international Rodrigo Isgró as one of four changes to their starting XV for Sunday’s EPCR Challenge Cup opener against RC Vannes at The Stoop.

The Gallagher PREM side will be aiming to kickstart their season after a challenging opening to the domestic campaign, with head coach Jason Gilmore making alterations to both his pack and backline ahead of the visit of the French outfit.

Rugby.title: Alisha Joyce returns to Bristol Bears on one-match deal five months after exit
Rugby.summary: Alisha Joyce has returned to Bristol Bears on a one-match deal, just five months after leaving the club.
bullets: Alisha Joyce has re-signed for Bristol Bears on a one-match deal, five months after leaving the club, for Saturday's JAECOO Next Gen Cup game against Harlequins at the Twickenham Stoop. The 29-year-old is named to start at lock alongside England and Ireland age-grade international Jorja Battishill. England hooker Lark Atkin-Davies also returns for the first time since giving birth to her daughter, Olive, 16 weeks ago.

Joyce left Bristol in May with her wife, Jasmine, citing the birth of their son, Ralphie, and their commute from Wales. Both are set to play in the 2026/27 Celtic Challenge, which begins in December, having represented Brython Thunder last season. Joyce came off the bench for Wales in September's 50-19 win over South Africa but was not picked for the tour of Japan. Bristol have won one of their two Next Gen Cup games, losing 28-24 to Trailfinders Women and beating Gloucester Hartpury 47-19.
Rugby.copy:
Alisha Joyce has returned to Bristol Bears on a one-match deal, just five months after leaving the club. The 29-year-old has re-signed for the West Country club for Saturday’s JAECOO Next Gen Cup encounter with Harlequins.

Joyce left Bristol in May alongside her wife, Jasmine, with the couple citing the birth of their son, Ralphie, and their commute from Wales as reasons for their departure. The pair are set to play in the 2026/27 Celtic Challenge, which begins in December, having both represented Brython Thunder last season.

Rugby.title: James Pater set for Champions Cup debut as Saints shake things up
Rugby.summary: Rising star James Pater is one of four Northampton players in line to make their Investec Champions Cup debuts after being named in the Saints' starting XV for the visit of Cardiff this Sunday.
bullets: Northampton have named four players in line to make their Investec Champions Cup debuts for Sunday's home game against Cardiff. Nineteen-year-old full-back James Pater, who has scored five tries in five appearances this season, starts at No.15, and Josh Taylor starts at openside. Prop Ion Neculai and back-row Charlie Ulcoq are set to make their debuts from the bench.

Ollie Sleightholme, who scored a hat-trick in last week's 71-48 win over Bath, and George Hendy join Pater in the back three, with Toby Thame and Rory Hutchinson in midfield. Anthony Belleau makes his first start of the season at fly-half alongside Alex Mitchell, and Callum Chick captains from No.8. Danilo Fischetti, Robbie Smith and Tom Lockett come into the pack, with Cleopas Kundiona and JJ Van Der Mescht retained.
Rugby.copy:
Rising star James Pater is one of four Northampton players in line to make their Investec Champions Cup debuts after being named in Saints’ starting XV for the visit of Cardiff this Sunday.

Pater, 19, who has scored five tries in five appearances from full-back this season, has been handed the No.15 jersey against the Welsh region after a string of impressive displays.

Rugby.title: Exeter Chiefs put 6'6 monster on wing against Toulouse in Champions Cup baptism of fire
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter gives rookie outside centre Zack Wimbush only his second appearance on the wing for the Investec Champions Cup trip to Top 14 champions Toulouse on Sunday afternoon.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs head coach Rob Baxter has given rookie outside centre Zack Wimbush only his second appearance on the wing for Sunday's Investec Champions Cup trip to Top 14 champions Toulouse. The change was forced after England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso suffered a hamstring injury in last weekend's first Gallagher PREM win of the season, against Newcastle Red Bulls. Olly Woodburn and Paul Brown-Bampoe are also out injured.

Tommy Wyatt starts on the other wing and Sam Harris at full-back, while Will Goodrick-Clarke makes his first start of the season at loosehead. Josh Iosefa-Scott leads the team out in his 100th club appearance, and Tom Hooper partners Dafydd Jenkins in the second row. Baxter said few challenges are greater than facing Toulouse, who have been French champions six times in eight years, and called for a bigger defensive work-rate than last weekend.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter gives rookie outside centre Zack Wimbush only his second appearance on the wing for the Investec Champions Cup trip to Top 14 champions Toulouse on Sunday afternoon.

Baxter has made the enforced change because England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso picked up a hamstring injury in their first Gallagher PREM win of the season against Newcastle Red Bulls last weekend.

Rugby.title: Joey Carbery to end Leinster exile as Leo Cullen makes 6 changes for Clermont
Rugby.summary: Leinster's prodigal son Joey Carbery is set for his first involvement since returning to the province after being named among the replacements for Saturday's Investec Champions Cup opener away to Clermont Auvergne.
bullets: Joey Carbery is named among the replacements for Leinster's Investec Champions Cup opener away to Clermont Auvergne on Saturday, in line for his first appearance since rejoining the province from Bordeaux Begles in the summer. It would be his first outing in Leinster blue since 2018. Leo Cullen has made six changes to the side that beat Cardiff 29-5 in the URC last weekend.

Dan Sheehan continues as captain at hooker, with Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong in the front row. Ryan Baird and Josh van der Flier join Jack Conan, who starts at No.8 for a second consecutive match, in the back row. Fintan Gunne partners Sam Prendergast at half-back, and Robbie Henshaw returns in midfield alongside Garry Ringrose. Hugo Keenan stays at full-back, with Tommy O'Brien and Jimmy O'Brien on the wings.
Rugby.copy:
Leinster’s prodigal son Joey Carbery is set for his first involvement since returning to the province after being named among the replacements for Saturday’s Investec Champions Cup opener away to Clermont Auvergne.

Leo Cullen has made six changes to the side that defeated Cardiff 29-5 in the URC last weekend, with Leinster travelling to Stade Marcel-Michelin for a daunting opening-round fixture against the French club.

Rugby.title: Ex-champ Sharks name depleted side for EPCR Challenge Cup trip to France
Rugby.summary: Former EPCR Challenge Cup winners the Sharks will begin their 2026/27 campaign with a significantly altered squad when they travel to France to face Lyon on Saturday.
bullets: The Sharks begin their 2026/27 EPCR Challenge Cup campaign away to Lyon on Saturday with a heavily altered side, as 16 squad members are unavailable. Those missing include Andre Esterhuizen, Bongi Mbonambi, Eben Etzebeth, Makazole Mapimpi, Ox Nche, Thomas du Toit and Trevor Nyakane. Head coach JP Pietersen has opted for a largely second-string selection.

Nick Hatton captains from No.8, and former Harlequins lock Stephan Lewies, who spent seven seasons in England, returns to the starting XV. Jordan Hendrikse recovers from injury to start at fly-half, with Jaco Williams back on the right wing. Forwards coach Warren Whiteley said the club places a lot of importance on the competition as past winners, and expects a physical Lyon side with a powerful pack and dangerous backs.
Rugby.copy:
Former EPCR Challenge Cup winners the Sharks will begin their 2026/27 campaign with a significantly altered squad when they travel to France to face Lyon on Saturday. The Durban outfit head into the opening pool-stage fixture without a host of Springboks and senior players, with 16 squad members unavailable for selection. Among those missing are Andre Esterhuizen, Bongi Mbonambi, Eben Etzebeth, Makazole Mapimpi, Ox Nche, Thomas du Toit and Trevor Nyakane.

As a result, head coach JP Pietersen has opted for a largely second-string selection. Nick Hatton will captain the side from No.8, while former Harlequins lock Stephan Lewies returns to the starting XV after making his comeback off the bench in last week’s VURC fixture. The experienced second-rower spent seven seasons in England and served as Harlequins captain for four years before returning to Durban.

Rugby.title: Double scrum-half boost for Bath as Spencer returns vs Montpellier
Rugby.summary: England international Spencer makes his first appearance of the season, having undergone shoulder surgery in the summer.
bullets: Bath have welcomed back club captain Ben Spencer and scrum-half Bernard van der Linde from injury for Saturday's Champions Cup home tie against Montpellier. England international Spencer makes his first appearance of the season after shoulder surgery in the summer, and starts alongside Finn Russell. South African van der Linde is on the bench, having recovered from the knock that kept him out of the heavy PREM defeat at Northampton last weekend.

Bath field an all-England international front row of Beno Obano, Tom Dunn and Will Stuart, with Will Jeanes making his European debut in the second row alongside Charlie Ewels. Ted Hill and Guy Pepper start on the flanks and Arthur Green at No.8. Charlie Griffin, who scored on his PREM debut last week, is set for his European debut on the left wing, with Joe Cokanasiga on the right and Santi Carreras at full-back.
Rugby.copy:
Bath welcome back two of their scrum-halves from injury, club captain Ben Spencer and Bernard van der Linde, for Saturday’s Champions Cup tie at home to Montpellier. England international Spencer makes his first appearance of the season, having undergone shoulder surgery in the summer, and starts the game alongside Finn Russell.

South African van der Linde provides cover for Spencer on the bench, having overcome the knock which saw him sit out the heavy PREM defeat at Northampton last weekend. Welcoming last year’s EPCR Challenge Cup winners to the Rec, Bath field an all-England international front row of Beno Obano, Tom Dunn and Will Stuart.

Rugby.title: Mick Cleary: 'This Champions Cup adventure is the perfect staging post for England’s best.'
Rugby.summary: England's club sides are playing with elan but after a weekend of Champions Cup action, Steve Borthwick will know more about their resolve
bullets: Mick Cleary writes that the opening weekend of the Investec Champions Cup is likely to bring more conservative scorelines than recent high-scoring PREM games, such as the 18-try match at Franklin's Gardens in which Northampton and Bath shared 119 points. He notes that Phil Dowson said he does not want games to be "basketball", and argues that ambition in attack is welcome as Steve Borthwick plans towards the World Cup. The last six Champions Cup titles have all been won by French teams.

Cleary says French squads are better resourced than PREM sides, which is reflected in squad depth. He highlights Gloucester's Friday-night Kingsholm test against defending champions Bordeaux, Section Paloise v Leicester Tigers, and Anglo-French ties for Bath and Exeter Chiefs. He says the true test for English teams is how they choose to attack the game, and that the competition is a stepping stone to Test-level intensity before the November Nations Championship matches.
Rugby.copy:
Au revoir le rugby du candyfloss. Bienvenue Europe and the real world. There is precious little chance of defences across the Investec Champions Cup being as accommodating as some have been in recent weeks in the PREM. While it’s true that attacking aristocrats such as Stade Toulousain and Union Bordeaux Begles could prise open Fort Knox RFC, there is a sense that scorelines are going to be of a more conservative format across this opening weekend of the competition, a welcome boon to the international coaches as they narrow their focus ahead of the impending month of Nations Championship matches in November.

Giddy scoreboards may be easy on the eye for casual viewers but they are the stuff of nightmares for defence coaches. The 18 try-fest at Franklin’s Gardens last Friday, with two of England’s finest Northampton Saints and Bath Rugby sharing 119 points, drew as much criticism as it did praise. For all the naysayers, there was much to take from the worldly-wise view of Phil Dowson who stated: “We don’t want it to be 99-88… we don’t want it to be basketball,’ before noting that basketball is actually one of the most well-watched sports in the United States as well as round the globe. It must be doing something right.

Rugby.title: Rugby Sevens Olympic dreams to be decided at the European Games 2027
Rugby.summary: Rugby Sevens Olympic dreams to be decided at the European Games 2027 Rugby Europe
bullets: Rugby Europe and the European Olympic Committees have announced that rugby sevens will feature at the fourth European Games in Istanbul, Türkiye, over four days from Wednesday 23 to Saturday 26 June 2027. The tournament expands from 12 to 16 teams following its debut in Kraków-Małopolska in 2023, where Ireland's men and Great Britain's women won and qualified for Paris 2024.

The 16 teams in each tournament qualified through the 2026 Rugby Europe 7s Championship and Trophy rankings, though lower-ranked teams could still enter depending on the HSBC SVNS season. The top four at the SVNS World Championship qualify for LA28, with the USA already qualified. If a European side finishes in the top four, the European Games spot goes to the next-ranked team. The SVNS series starts in Dubai in November and finishes in Bordeaux in May 2027.
Rugby.copy:
Rugby Europe and the European Olympic Committees (EOC) have announced that Rugby Sevens will once again be included in the fourth edition of the European Games, taking place in Istanbul, Türkiye in 2027.

It will be the second time that the sport has featured in the European Games following a successful debut in Kraków-Małopolska in 2023, where Ireland's men and Great Britain's women won the tournaments and subsequently qualified for Paris 2024.

Rugby.title: Archie van der Flier's form prompts questions about Test allegiance
Rugby.summary: A few years ago, van der Flier was playing uni rugby for Nottingham, whilst appearing for the city's Champ side on loan from Leicester's senior academy.
bullets: Leicester loosehead Archie van der Flier, 24, won the TNT Sports Player of the Match award in last weekend's 38-31 win over Gloucester, which was his first PREM start. He was picked ahead of Mako Vunipola after making 21 bench appearances in his breakthrough season, and passed an HIA after an early mouthguard trigger. He said Nicky Smith, who started every PREM game for two seasons, had been ahead of him last season.

A surprise England A cap in February, against an Ireland XV, has prompted talk of senior international honours, either with England or alongside his 82-cap cousin Josh van der Flier for Ireland, for whom he qualifies through his Irish father. England A are understood to be England's 'capture' team, making him ineligible for Ireland until a stand-down period has elapsed. Leicester play Pau away on Sunday, and Leinster in Round 4 on 16 January, with Archie saying the squad is determined to go for the tournament, 17 years after their last European final.
Rugby.copy:
Given that Archie van der Flier was virtually a permanent fixture in Leicester’s run to the playoffs in 2025/26, one of the more surprising stats of last weekend was the fact that the 38-31 win against Gloucester was his first-ever PREM start.

Selected in the number one jersey ahead of Mako Vunipola, the loosehead, who made 21 bench appearances in his breakthrough season, overcame an early setback to join the select group of props to have won the TNT Sports’ Player of the Match award.

Rugby.title: ‘She is now the biggest why in my life’: Lark Atkin-Davies on motherhood and rugby return
Rugby.summary: Lark Atkin-Davies will return to the rugby pitch this Saturday for Bristol after having her daughter Olive and she credits support, the RFU's maternity policy and Abbie Ward for her becoming a mother alongside her rugby career.
bullets: England hooker Lark Atkin-Davies, 31, returns to the pitch for Bristol against Harlequins in Saturday's PWR NextGen Cup, 16 weeks after giving birth to her daughter, Olive. She last played in the Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 final. She credits support at Bristol and the Red Roses, the RFU's maternity policy and her teammate Abbie Ward, who returned to the pitch after having her daughter, Hallie.

Atkin-Davies trained until the week before giving birth and was back training two weeks after. She managed gestational diabetes with insulin, which required a therapeutic use exemption as it is a prohibited substance in rugby, and said being a sportsperson helped her handle the diagnosis. She had thought in 2019 she might give up rugby to have a family, but her husband Jamie's move to self-employed work as a financial adviser made childcare more flexible.
Rugby.copy:
Lark Atkin-Davies will return to the rugby pitch this Saturday for Bristol after having her daughter Olive and she credits support, the RFU’s maternity policy and Abbie Ward for her becoming a mother alongside her rugby career.

The England international, who last played in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final, had initially thought she would give up the sport to have a family when she was first awarded a professional contract in 2019. Since then maternity policy has evolved for the Red Roses and she also saw her Bristol and England teammate Ward have her first daughter, Hallie, and return to the pitch.

The Sale Sharks centre partners Blagnac's Alyssa D'Incà in midfield, with Alia Bitonci and Emma Stevanin at half-back and Benetton Rugby Treviso flanker Mascia Jelic making her debut in the back row.

The USA enter the home leg of their WXV Global Series campaign having beaten Ireland and Wales in Europe. Added to their July win over the Springbok Women, those results give the Eagles three consecutive Test victories for the first time since 2006, and they are targeting a fourth. Head coach Jack Hanratty said closing out two Tests had brought confidence to the group, adding that the aim is a world-class squad rather than just a world-class team.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: New Zealand Rugby statement: Court ruling in row over NRL team's name
Rugby.summary: New Zealand Rugby have issued a statement following a High Court ruling as they bid to block the use of the "Chiefs" name by a new Papua New Guinea-based rugby league franchise.
bullets: New Zealand Rugby has responded to a High Court decision declining an interim injunction against the use of the "Chiefs" name by a new Papua New Guinea-based rugby league franchise. The ruling clears the way for the PNG Chiefs brand launch on 21 October, ahead of the club's entry to the NRL from the 2028 season.

NZR said the decision relates only to the interim injunction, is not a ruling on the merits of its case, and that its application for a final injunction remains before the Court. It argues two teams called the Chiefs in similar codes and the same commercial markets would cause confusion, citing protections in place since 1998. The ARLC made commitments to the Court to take active steps to avoid confusion in New Zealand, while Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis called the ruling "an early step".
Rugby.copy:
New Zealand Rugby have issued a statement following a High Court ruling as they bid to block the use of the “Chiefs” name by a new Papua New Guinea-based rugby league franchise.

The High Court has declined to grant an interim injunction, clearing the way for the PNG Chiefs brand launch later this month, although NZR insists the ruling does not address the merits of its trademark case.

Cyprus, who set a world record of 24 consecutive wins between 2008 and 2014, have lost their last four Tests. Gibraltar head coach Lee Fortey said his focus is on his own team, though they are without lock Matt Scott and prop Tommy Grimes through injury. Rugby.title: How a new Champions Cup campaign brings the same old problems
Rugby.summary: Few are happy with the competition format or calendar – but, as Harry Latham-Coyle explains, necessary changes may not be imminent
bullets: The new Investec Champions Cup campaign begins with 24 teams and a familiar structure: a one-week window in October followed by a two-month pause, with the competition picking up in earnest in the New Year. Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan likened the Champions Cup and Gallagher Prem to a sprint and a marathon, noting that even Bordeaux, back-to-back winners, did not finish in the Top 14's top six.

There is widespread agreement that the competition needs a revamp, with a 16-team format preferred by most, but contracts run until 2030 and the proposed Club World Cup appears shelved. Premier Sports' UK broadcast deal is in its final year, with hope that TNT Sports may return. Saracens' Jamie George said it is harder for English teams to compete, and the attacking bonus point now requires three more tries than the opposition. The final is in Lyon next May.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Perhaps it was Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, who best summed up the difficulty of challenging in both the Investec Champions Cup and Gallagher Prem when he compared the two competitions to a sprint and a marathon respectively. Any runner will tell you that it is very hard to be good at each; a sacrifice has to be made somewhere.

It is a lesson that Van Graan and his side learned last year – losing semi-finalists both domestically and in Europe, a season that promised plenty for a club with dynastic aspirations ultimately delivered little.

Rugby.title: Munster to remember 'special' Foley 10 years after his death
Rugby.summary: Denis Leamy, Tadhg Beirne and Peter O'Mahony speak about Anthony Foley as Munster prepare to honour their former captain and head coach on the 10th anniversary of his death.
bullets: Munster will pay tribute to Anthony Foley at Pairc Ui Chaoimh in Cork on Saturday, in their Investec Champions Cup game against Racing 92, ten years after his death. Foley, then Munster head coach, died suddenly in his sleep aged 42 in Paris ahead of a match against Racing, after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs. The players will wear commemorative jackets featuring the club crest and the number eight, with a rendition of 'There Is An Isle', a photo display in Marina Park and a round of applause in the eighth minute.

Foley captained Munster to the 2006 Heineken Cup, won 62 Ireland caps and made 201 Munster appearances, 86 of them in Europe. Defence coach Denis Leamy said his memory is "to the forefront of everyone's mind", while captain Tadhg Beirne said Foley's quotes are still spoken about around the club. Munster played Glasgow a week after his death and won 38-17, and former captain Peter O'Mahony described the period as probably the toughest of his life.
Rugby.copy:
European nights are invariably significant occasions for Munster, but this Saturday will be especially poignant as they remember one of the greats. Friday marks 10 years since the death of Anthony Foley. With Munster in Paris before facing Racing 92, Foley - head coach at the time - died suddenly in his sleep aged 42 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs.

Having captained Munster to the 2006 Heineken Cup during a stellar playing career that also yielded 62 Ireland caps, the outpouring of grief that followed his passing was remarkable.

Racket.title: Elena Rybakina outlines her main WTA Tour goal for the rest of the 2026 season
Racket.summary: Rybakina is set for Ningbo Open action. The post Elena Rybakina outlines her main WTA Tour goal for the rest of the 2026 season appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: World No 1 Elena Rybakina has said her main goal for the rest of the 2026 season is to finish the year as number one, while managing her health and fitness. She has not won a match since lifting the US Open title in September, losing her opening match at the China Open to Alina Charaeva. She faces the winner of Cristina Bucsa and Polina Kudermetova in the second round of the Ningbo Open.

Rybakina will then defend her WTA Finals title, which she won by beating Jessica Pegula and Aryna Sabalenka in the knockout rounds. No player has won back-to-back titles since Serena Williams in 2013 and 2014. This year's event is at Indian Wells, moving from Riyadh, from 8 to 15 November. Gauff, Sabalenka, Andreeva, Noskova, Svitolina and Pegula have also qualified.
Racket.copy:
Elena Rybakina has undoubtedly been the best player on the WTA Tour this year stastically, but she has produced some strange performances and endured some strange results. The star is yet to taste victory since lifting the US Open title in September, having lost her opening round match at the China Open to Alina Charaeva.

That was not the only early exit Rybakina has suffered in 2026 either, as she was beaten in the opening round of the Berlin Open and the second round of Roland Garros. Rybakina is looking to return to winning ways at the Ningbo Open, which is the penultimate WTA 500 tournament of the 2026 season.

Racket.title: Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
Racket.summary: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.
bullets: Ukrainian tennis player Elina Svitolina, 32 and ranked sixth in the world, has announced the end of her marriage to French former player Gaël Monfils, 40. In an Instagram post she cited the emotional impact of the war in Ukraine, saying she needs to find her way back to herself and could not do so within the marriage.

Svitolina said Monfils listened and respected her needs with strength and grace. The couple married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai, who Svitolina said will always come first, adding that the marriage is ending but the family is not. She grew up in Odesa, which has been heavily bombed by Russia since its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Racket.copy:
Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player Gaël Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country.

The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside". "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage.

Racket.title: Carlos Alcaraz’s next Davis Cup coach confirmed after David Ferrer’s departure
Racket.summary: It's someone Carlos Alcaraz knows well. The post Carlos Alcaraz’s next Davis Cup coach confirmed after David Ferrer’s departure appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: David Ferrer has announced that the 2026 Davis Cup will be his last as Spain captain after four years in charge, citing solely personal reasons and a desire to start a new stage. Marc Lopez, already part of the Spain Davis Cup setup, will take over the team from 2027.

Spain have not won the Davis Cup under Ferrer, but are among the favourites at this year's Finals in Bologna from 24 to 29 November, where they will compete against South Korea, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Austria, Czech Republic and Canada. Alejandro Davidovich Fokina and Rafael Jodar, who both reached the Shanghai Masters final, are in contention for selection alongside Carlos Alcaraz, Marcel Granollers and Pedro Martinez. Spain last won the title in 2019.
Racket.copy:
David Ferrer confirmed the 2026 Davis Cup would be his final year in charge of Spain after four years in charge. “I wanted to announce that this will be my last year as Davis Cup captain, giving up the year 2027. I want to thank the RFET for the opportunity it gave me to fulfil one of my dreams, which is to be able to be Davis Cup captain of my country,” said Ferrer in a social media post.

“I also want to thank all the players and all the people who have accompanied me during this adventure. It has been a privilege to share this journey with all of them. The reasons for this decision are solely personal and respond to the desire to be able to start a new stage.

Racket.title: Alex Eala climbs in WTA Rankings as she ends losing streak with dominant Ningbo Open win
Racket.summary: Eala dropped just four games as she earned her first win since the Asian Games. The post Alex Eala climbs in WTA Rankings as she ends losing streak with dominant Ningbo Open win appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alex Eala ended a losing run with a 6-3, 6-1 first-round win over world No 34 Diane Parry at the Ningbo Open, a WTA 500 event, on Monday. The 21-year-old broke Parry six times, three in each set, and won 56 of the 91 points, with 12 winners to nine unforced errors.

Eala had lost her previous two matches, a first-round exit in Wuhan following her Asian Games semi-final defeat, and had lost three straight at WTA Tour level. The result lifts her two places from world No 20 to No 18 in the Live WTA Rankings, with 2,241 points. She will next face either sixth seed Diana Shnaider or qualifier Yulia Putintseva.
Racket.copy:
Alex Eala ended her losing streak with a dominant first round victory at the 2026 Ningbo Open, and she is projected to move up in the WTA Rankings. The Filipina star defeated world No 34 Diane Parry 6-3, 6-1 on the opening day of the WTA 500 tournament in Ningbo on Monday.

After Parry held in her first two service games, Eala broke the 24-year-old Frenchwoman six consecutive times — three times in each set — as she surged to the finish line. Eala was broken just twice and won 56 of the 91 points in a one-sided contest, while she recorded an impressive ratio of 12 winners to nine unforced errors.

Racket.title: Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Jannik Sinner concerns expose glaring omission in ATP proposals
Racket.summary: "It’s getting in the wrong direction." The post Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Jannik Sinner concerns expose glaring omission in ATP proposals appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi's 'OneVision' proposals include more than doubling the Bonus Pool for the top 30 players, raising the importance of Masters events in ranking points and increasing central player compensation from 2028. They form part of a $350million financial injection and also cover calendar reform, doubles players and incentives.

The proposals did not address the two-week Masters 1000 format, which Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have criticised, while Jannik Sinner has said he prefers one-week events. Doubles players have also criticised plans that could halve their draws from 2028, with their share of prize money potentially falling from 20% to 10%.
Racket.copy:
The ATP Tour’s ‘OneVision’ proposals appear to have been well received but there is one glaring issue that has not been addressed by chairman Andrea Gaudenzi. In a candid Q&A, Gaudenzi spoke about more than doubling the Bonus Pool for tennis’ top-30 ranked players, increasing the prestige and importance of Masters events when it comes to ranking points, and upping central player compensation from 2028.

The topics of calendar reform, doubles players facing an uncertain future, and changing incentives were also discussed, as part of a $350million financial injection, but one matter was, arguably, conspicuously absent.

bullets: Maja Chwalinska rose 11 places to a new career-high world No 11 after beating Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in the Wuhan Open final on Sunday. Kartal began the week ranked 170th, playing on a protected ranking, and climbed 121 places to 49th, five below her career-best of 44th.

Jelena Ostapenko moved up 10 places to 24th, and Ann Li climbed six to a career-high 25th. World No 1 Elena Rybakina missed Wuhan with a foot injury and dropped 500 points, allowing Aryna Sabalenka to close the gap to 1,646 points. Bianca Andreescu jumped 36 places to 132nd after winning the Rovereto Challenger.
Racket.copy:
Maja Chwalinska and Sonay Kartal faced off in a surprise final at the 2026 Wuhan Open, and they have both made significant jumps in the WTA Rankings. Polish star Chwalinska downed Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in the title match at the WTA 1000 tournament in Wuhan on Sunday.

Chwalinska, who was a runner-up at Roland Garros in June, has jumped 11 places to a new career-high ranking of world No 11 following her maiden career title. Kartal started Wuhan as the world No 170 and competed using a protected ranking after missing over six months this season due to injury.

Racket.title: Novak Djokovic tipped for ATP Finals twist as Rafael Jodar and Alex De Minaur sent late warning
Racket.summary: "This has added a little more intrigue to the ATP Tour right now." The post Novak Djokovic tipped for ATP Finals twist as Rafael Jodar and Alex De Minaur sent late warning appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Greg Rusedski has said he would not be surprised to see Novak Djokovic reach the ATP Finals in Turin, even though the 39-year-old currently sits outside the qualification places. Djokovic is 11th in the Race on 2,840 points after an early exit at the Shanghai Masters, while Rafael Jodar is ninth on 3,159 and Alex De Minaur is 10th on 2,880. With world No 1 Jannik Sinner out for the rest of the season, ninth place is enough to qualify.

Rusedski said on Off Court with Greg Rusedski that Djokovic is only around 200 points behind Jodar and has a strong record at the Paris Masters, where he is a seven-time champion. The Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia has been postponed until December, and Djokovic has taken a late wildcard for the ATP 500 event in Basel later this month. Several rivals, including Flavio Cobolli, Tommy Paul, Arthur Fils and Daniil Medvedev, are in action this week.
Racket.copy:
Greg Rusedski would not be surprised to see Novak Djokovic sneak into the ATP Finals despite currently sitting outside the qualification spots. After his remarkable China Open triumph, Djokovic was well set to qualify for the season-ending event in Turin but things have changed quickly since then.

The 39-year-old’s early exit at the Shanghai Masters opened the door for the likes of Alex De Minaur and Rafael Jodar to overtake him in the Race. After Alejandro Davidovich Fokina’s stunning victory at the Masters 1000 event, where he beat Jodar in three sets in the final, Djokovic is currently 11th in the Race on 2,840 points.

bullets: World No 6 Elina Svitolina has announced she has separated from her husband Gaël Monfils. In an Instagram post, the 32-year-old Ukrainian described the toll of Russia's war against her country and said she could not rediscover herself within the marriage. The couple married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai.

Svitolina said there was no one to blame and that the marriage was ending but the family was not. Monfils, 40, a former world No 6 with 13 career titles, appears to have brought forward his retirement, which had been expected after a farewell outing at the Paris Masters starting on 31 October. He now appears on the International Tennis Integrity Agency's list of retired players.
Racket.copy:
The world No 6 Elina Svitolina has announced she has separated from her husband Gaël Monfils. In an emotional Instagram post, the 32-year-old Ukrainian opened up about the mental toll of Russia’s war against her country, describing sleepless nights and self-doubt. Svitolina said she had come to realise she needed to rediscover herself and could no longer do so within her marriage.

“This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,” she wrote. “Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside. With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.

Racket.title: World Junior Championships 2026: Sow wins bronze, Indonesia top medal table
Racket.summary: World Junior Championships 2026: Sow wins bronze, Indonesia top medal table Badminton Europe
bullets: The VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 ended in Cairo, with Europe winning one bronze medal. France's Mady Sow, the 16-year-old top seed, lost in three games in the semi-finals to Indonesia's Fardhan Rainanda Joe, and became only the third French player to medal at the event after Alex Lanier and Christo Popov. Czechia's Vojtěch Strejček and Lukáš Thor reached the quarter-finals.

Indonesia topped the medal table with two titles. Radithya Bayu Wardhana won an all-Indonesian men's singles final 15-9 11-15 15-8 over Joe, and Muhammad Luthfi Habibi and Dian Ramadhani Mukti saved three match points to win the mixed doubles. China's Zhang Yi Xin won the women's singles, while Chinese Taipei's Chen Ping Hsuan and Lee Wei Ting took the men's doubles and Malaysia's Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim won the women's doubles.
Racket.copy:
The VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 have come to a close in Cairo, and Europe heads home with a bronze medal. Czechia’s Vojtěch Strejček/Lukáš Thor made it through to the quarterfinals. France’s Mady Sow went one step further. The 16-year-old top seed reached the semifinals, where he lost in three games to Indonesia’s Fardhan Rainanda Joe. Sow’s bronze makes him only the third French player to win a medal at the event, after Alex Lanier and Christo Popov.

Joe went on to the men’s singles final, which was an all-Indonesian clash. Radithya Bayu Wardhana took the title 15-9 11-15 15-8. In women’s singles, China’s Zhang Yi Xin won against Japan’s Saki Matsumoto 9-15 15-10 15-9. Chinese Taipei’s Chen Ping Hsuan/Lee Wei Ting won the men’s doubles 15-10 15-9 against Japan’s Mahiro Oku/Masato Yamashiro, which was Chinese Taipei’s first gold in a doubles event at these championships.

Racket.copy:

Racket.title: Novak Djokovic, Marta Kostyuk, Naomi Osaka and more react to Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils’ surprise split
Racket.summary: Tennis stars send messages of support to Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils following news of their split. The post Novak Djokovic, Marta Kostyuk, Naomi Osaka and more react to Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils’ surprise split appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Tennis players have reacted on social media to Elina Svitolina's announcement that her marriage to Gael Monfils is ending after more than five years. Novak Djokovic, Stan Wawrinka and Linda Noskova liked her Instagram post, while Marta Kostyuk and Naomi Osaka left heart emojis in the comments.

Svitolina said the pair will continue to co-parent their daughter Skai, born in late 2022, and that she needs to find her way back to herself. The couple began dating in 2019 and married two years later. The announcement follows Monfils quietly retiring just before his planned final tournament at the Paris Masters, and he has said he will start a career in finance.
Racket.copy:
Tennis stars have reacted to the news of Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils’ surprise split after more than five years of marriage. In an emotional statement, Svitolina said her marriage to the Frenchman is ending, but “our family is not”. The world No 6 revealed the two will continue to co-parent their daughter Skai, who was born in late 2022, but she needs to “find my way back to myself”.

Svitolina has been an outspoken critic of Russia following its invasion of Ukraine in early 2022, and it seems the war continues to take its toll on her. Part of her statement reads, “It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gaël listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget.

Racket.copy:

Racket.title: Elina Svitolina announces shock split from Gael Monfils in emotional statement – ‘I need to find my way back to myself’
Racket.summary: "The hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love." The post Elina Svitolina announces shock split from Gael Monfils in emotional statement – ‘I need to find my way back to myself’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Elina Svitolina has announced on Instagram that her marriage to Gael Monfils is ending, saying she needs to find her way back to herself. The couple began dating in 2019, married in summer 2021 and have a daughter, Skai, born in late 2022. The 32-year-old world No 6 said there was no one to blame and asked for space to heal.

Svitolina said she had struggled with the war's effect on her, and noted that last September she ended her season early after not feeling like herself. Monfils, 40, quietly retired from tennis earlier this month, ahead of what was due to be his final tournament at the Paris Masters. The pair played mixed doubles together at the US Open in late August.
Racket.copy:
Elina Svitolina has announced that her marriage to Gael Monfils is ending as she needs to “find my way back to myself”. Svitolina and Monfils began dating in 2019 before marrying in the summer of 2021. In late 2022, the couple announced the birth of daughter Skai, and it seems all was well behind the scenes.

However, the Ukrainian star took to Instagram on Monday to announce that the couple would be parting ways, but “our family is not”. The 32-year-old said despite all of Monfils‘ support, “some battles happen deep inside you,” and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you.

Racket.title: Forgotten ATP star opens up on ‘depression and burnout’ after rankings collapse
Racket.summary: "These past few months have certainly been difficult." The post Forgotten ATP star opens up on ‘depression and burnout’ after rankings collapse appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Former world No 29 Giovanni Mpetschi Perricard has told L'Equipe he has experienced "a little depression, burnout" after a sharp fall down the rankings. The 23-year-old Frenchman reached 31st in the world in 2024 and won his first ATP Tour titles in Lyon and Basel. This year his tour record is 8-18, he has no Grand Slam match win and he has dropped to 145th after losing in the first round of qualifying in Brussels.

Mpetschi Perricard said he was left without a coach after the US Open, played only once every two or three days and stopped watching tennis, with friends helping him through the period. He is on an eight-match losing streak, including defeats to world No 227 Remy Bertola and No 817 Etienne Donnet. He was coached earlier this year by Greg Rusedski, and said he must persevere and change his mindset, believing things will work out over time.
Racket.copy:
Former top-30 player Giovanni Mpetschi Perricard has opened up on his “depression and burnout” after sliding down the rankings. The big Frenchman enjoyed a breakthrough year in 2024, rising to 31st in the world and picking up his first ATP Tour titles in Lyon and Basel.

The 6ft 7in player beat the likes of Felix Auger-Aliassime, Holger Rune, and Ben Shelton at the Swiss Indoors, as his booming serve proved too hot to handle. Just when it seemed like the then 21-year-old, who holds the record for the fastest serve at Wimbledon at 153mph, would become the next big thing in French tennis, Mpetschi Perricard‘s progress has come to a grinding halt.

Racket.title: Inside British number one Kartal's remarkable comeback
Racket.summary: Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not brush her teeth without "being in agony" - now she's the British number one after three events back from a long-term back injury.
bullets: Sonay Kartal, 24, became British number one on Monday after reaching the Wuhan Open final in only her third tournament back from a stress fracture in her back. Using a protected ranking, she rose from 170th to 49th by earning 650 points, and became the first British player to reach a WTA 1000 final since Johanna Konta in 2019. She lost the final to French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Kartal said she was unable to walk without pain for about the first month of her injury and credited coach Ben Reeves, fitness coach Ian Aylward and physio Dani Gillanders. Regaining her ranking means she will no longer need a protected ranking for events including the 2027 Australian Open. She withdrew from the Japan Open in Osaka, saying the goals of her Asian swing had been achieved.
Racket.copy:
Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not stand up and brush her teeth without "being in agony". The pain caused by a stress fracture in her back eventually subsided, but the 24-year-old Briton still had a long road to full recovery, which needed to be navigated with patience and hard work.

Kartal did not make her return to competitive action until little under a month ago. But on Monday, she became the new British number one after an extraordinary week at the Wuhan Open, where she reached the biggest final of her career in just her third tournament back.

Racket.title: Sonay Kartal: What next for new British No 1 after 'unbelievable week' in run to the final at Wuhan Open
Racket.summary: Sonay Kartal: What next for new British No 1 after 'unbelievable week' in run to the final at Wuhan Open Sky Sports
bullets: Sonay Kartal became the new British No 1 after reaching the Wuhan Open final, where she lost 2-6 6-4 6-2 to Poland's Maja Chwalinska. She became only the second Briton after Johanna Konta to play a WTA 1000 final, beating Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko along the way.

The 24-year-old had returned only last month after six months out with a stress fracture in her back, which forced her to retire from the fourth round at Indian Wells in March. She can use her protected ranking for 12 months, and may withdraw from the Japan Open in Osaka before ending her season at WTA 500 or 250 events in China, Hong Kong and India.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal enjoyed the best week of her career so far as she surprisingly made the final at the Wuhan Open; Kartal only recently returned from injury, so what is her potential and can she kick on? Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis

Sonay Kartal is the new British No 1 after her remarkable run to the Wuhan Open final where she was narrowly beaten by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in three sets. Kartal became just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to play in a WTA 1000 final with superb wins over Tokyo Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini, world No 6 Elina Svitolina and former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko.

Racket.title: Denmark Says Thank You to Axelsen
Racket.summary: Denmark Says Thank You to Axelsen BWF
bullets: Danish badminton paid tribute to Viktor Axelsen in his home city of Odense on Sunday at the SJF Bank Arena, where he was presented with flowers. Odense Mayor Peter Rahbaek Juel and Badminton Denmark Chief Executive Kristian Pihl delivered tributes, with Pihl thanking Axelsen for the journey, the memories and everything he had given Danish badminton.

Axelsen's achievements include two Olympic gold medals, two world titles, four European crowns and a place in the Danish team that won the country's first Thomas Cup in 2016. He also spent years at the top of the world rankings in men's singles. Thanking fans, sponsors, family and friends, he said he started playing in Odense and almost hit his last shuttlecock there as well.
Racket.copy:
Danish badminton paid tribute to its greatest modern player Viktor Axelsen in his home city of Odense on Sunday. At the SJF Bank Arena, Axelsen was presented with flowers before receiving heartfelt tributes from the Mayor of Odense Peter Rahbaek Juel and Badminton Denmark Chief Executive Kristian Pihl. Their message was simple.

“We have come together to say thank you,” said Pihl. “Thank you, Viktor for the journey, the memories and everything you have given Danish badminton.” For nearly two decades, Axelsen carried Danish hopes on the biggest stages in world sports. He became a global ambassador for badminton, inspired a new generation of players and built a legacy few can match.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: An-Stoppable Force
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: An-Stoppable Force BWF World Tour
bullets: An Se Young won her 47th international title at the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026, beating Akane Yamaguchi 21-23 21-14 21-18 in the final. The world No.1 trailed 11-5 at the interval of the deciding game before taking 11 of the next 12 points. The win made her the most decorated women's singles player in international badminton, one title clear of Indonesia's Susi Susanti.

An, 24, slipped during the second game and said she would check her condition and speak to her trainer before deciding what to do next. She said the slower side of the court in the decider helped her confidence. She has now faced Yamaguchi 39 times and described her as her best rival, also naming Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei as rivals.
Racket.copy:
Down 11-5 at the decider’s interval, An Se Young looked destined to wait another week for her landmark victory. Then, in that moment of doubt, the champion fans know best emerged.

Eleven of the next 12 points fell her way and suddenly there was no stopping the world No.1 from claiming her 47th title. The triumph, a hard-fought 21-23 21-14 21-18 victory over Akane Yamaguchi in the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 final, made her the most decorated women’s singles player in international badminton, moving one title clear of Indonesian great Susi Susanti.

Racket.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My parents were very hard to please, but it shaped my resilience” - How Emma
Racket.summary: Inspiring story of the day: “My parents were very hard to please, but it shaped my resilience” - How Emma The Times of India
bullets: Emma Raducanu won the 2021 US Open at the age of 18 without dropping a set in 10 matches, becoming the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title. She won three qualifying matches and seven main-draw rounds, beating Greece's Maria Sakkari in the semi-finals and Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 6-3 in the final.

Raducanu has said her strict upbringing in Bromley, south London, built her resilience. Her Romanian father Ian and Chinese mother Renee Zhai, both of whom worked in finance, set high expectations, and she earned an A* in mathematics and an A in economics at A-level in 2021. She said her parents' limits on her social life left her comfortable in her own company, and credits her mother's 'step by step' advice for her calmness.
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu made tennis history at 18 when she won the 2021 US Open without dropping a set in 10 matches, becoming the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title. Her success came after years of balancing tennis training with schoolwork and living under her parents’ high expectations. Born in Toronto to Romanian father Ian Raducanu and Chinese mother Renee Zhai, she moved to England as a young child. Raducanu has often spoken about how her strict upbringing helped her become more independent, focused and resilient.

How did Ian Raducanu and Renee Zhai shape Emma Raducanu’s childhood? Emma Raducanu grew up in Bromley, south London, in a family that placed a strong focus on education and hard work. Her father, Ian, is Romanian, while her mother, Renee, is Chinese. Both worked in finance and encouraged their daughter to take her responsibilities seriously, both in the classroom and on the tennis court.

Racket.title: Alex Lanier wins Denmark Open 2026
Racket.summary: Alex Lanier wins Denmark Open 2026 Badminton Europe
bullets: Alex Lanier won the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 in his first tournament since becoming World Champion, beating home favourite Anders Antonsen 21-15, 13-21, 21-13 in an all-European final. The Frenchman took the opening game, Antonsen levelled in the second, and Lanier then raised his intensity in the decider.

Lanier said the third game required more physicality, aggressiveness and pace, and admitted the title was a surprise. Antonsen, who had won the Arctic Open the previous Sunday before reaching his third Denmark Open final, said he was proud but also sad and disappointed. The BWF World Tour continues with the French Open 2026, a Super 750 event in Paris starting on Tuesday, 20 October.
Racket.copy:
Alex Lanier claimed the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 title in his first tournament since becoming World Champion, defeating home favourite Anders Antonsen 21-15, 13-21, 21-13 in an all-European final.

The Frenchman took the opening game, but Antonsen responded strongly in the second to force a decider. With the title at stake, Lanier raised his intensity and eventually secured another major triumph.
